6.13.d: उत्तरेण सदो गत्वा ब्रह्मा अपरया द्वारा सदस् प्रपद्य दक्षिणेन मैत्रावरुणम् गत्वा यथा आसनम् आस्ते ।
6.13.m: Having gone north of the sadas, having entered the sadas through the western door, and having gone south of the Maitrāvaruṇa, the Brahman sits down in his seat.

6.13.s: na asaṃsthite savane aparayā dvārā nihsarpanti |
6.13.d: न असंस्थिते सवने अपरया द्वारा निह्सर्पन्ति ।
6.13.m: While the pressing has not concluded, they do not creep out through the western door.

6.13.s: antareṇa hotur maitrāvaruṇasya ca dhiṣṇyāv adhiṣṇyānām visaṃsthita saṃcaraḥ |
6.13.d: अन्तरेण होतुर् मैत्रावरुणस्य च धिष्ण्याव् अधिष्ण्यानाम् विसंस्थित संचरः ।
6.13.m: Between the dhiṣṇyas of the Hotṛ and the Maitrāvaruṇa is the passage for those without dhiṣṇyas while [the rite] is unfinished.
For those possessing dhiṣṇyas, [the passage is] north of their respective dhiṣṇya.
[The passage is] northward by the western half of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth,
or southward by that of the Mārjālīya.
And without turning round, they return.

6.13.s: āditya upasthānam rātri paryāyeṣv āśvine ca na vidyate na vidyate |
6.13.d: आदित्य उपस्थानम् रात्रि पर्यायेष्व् आश्विने च न विद्यते न विद्यते ।
6.13.m: Attendance upon the sun is not found during the night rounds and the Āśvina [śastra], is not found.

7.1.m: Having glided forward, they proceed with the press-cakes.
‘Rich in parched grain’ is the introductory verse.

7.1.s: hotā yakṣad indrma harivān ity anusavanam praiṣo yathā samāmnātam |
7.1.d: होता यक्षद् इन्द्र्म हरिवान् इत्य् अनुसवनम् प्रैषो यथा समाम्नातम् ।
7.1.m: ‘Let the Hotṛ worship Indra accompanied by bay steeds’ is the ritual summons for each pressing, according to the traditional text.
He stretches it out according to each pressing.

7.1.s: tena eva yajaty uddhṛtya hotā ayakṣam hotar yajam ca |
7.1.d: तेन एव यजत्य् उद्धृत्य होता अयक्षम् होतर् यजम् च ।
7.1.m: With that very [formula] he recites the offering verse, omitting ‘the Hotṛ has sacrificed’ and ‘Hotṛ, sacrifice’.

7.1.s: agne juṣasva no havir iti sviṣṭakṛtaḥ puronuvākyā |
7.1.d: अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविर् इति स्विष्टकृतः पुरोनुवाक्या ।
7.1.m: ‘O Agni, enjoy our oblation’ is the introductory verse of the Sviṣṭakṛt.

7.1.s: hotā yakṣad agni puroḷāśānām ity anusavanam praiṣaiḥ |
7.1.d: होता यक्षद् अग्नि पुरोऌआशानाम् इत्य् अनुसवनम् प्रैषैः ।
7.1.m: ‘Let the Hotṛ worship Agni of the sacrificial cakes’ is the ritual summons for each pressing.

7.1.s: havir agne vīhi iti ca yājyā |
7.1.d: हविर् अग्ने वीहि इति च याज्या ।
7.1.m: And ‘Agni, enjoy the oblation’ is the consecratory verse.

7.2.s: aindravāyava maitrāvaruṇāv āśvinaś ca dvi devatyāḥ |
7.2.d: ऐन्द्रवायव मैत्रावरुणाव् आश्विनश् च द्वि देवत्याः ।
7.2.m: The cups for Indra-Vāyu, for Mitra-Varuṇa, and for the Aśvins are the two-deity cups.

7.2.s: vāyav ā yāhi darśata indra vāyū ima ity aindra vāyavasya puronuvākye |
7.2.d: वायव् आ याहि दर्शत इन्द्र वायू इम इत्य् ऐन्द्र वायवस्य पुरोनुवाक्ये ।
7.2.m: ‘Come, O Vāyu, lovely to behold’ and ‘O Indra and Vāyu, these [somas]’ are the two introductory verses for the cup for Indra-Vāyu.

7.2.s: hotā yakṣad vāyum hotā yakṣad indra vāyū iti praiṣau |
7.2.d: होता यक्षद् वायुम् होता यक्षद् इन्द्र वायू इति प्रैषौ ।
7.2.m: ‘Let the Hotṛ worship Vāyu’ and ‘Let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Vāyu’ are the two ritual summonses.

7.2.s: agram piba śatenā na iti yājye |
7.2.d: अग्रम् पिब शतेना न इति याज्ये ।
7.2.m: ‘Drink the first’ and ‘With a hundred’ are the two consecratory verses.

7.2.s: ayam vām mitrāvaruṇā iti maitrāvaruṇasya puronuvākyā |
7.2.d: अयम् वाम् मित्रावरुणा इति मैत्रावरुणस्य पुरोनुवाक्या ।
7.2.m: ‘This to you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa’ is the introductory verse for the cup for Mitra-Varuṇa.

7.2.s: hotā yakṣan mitrā varuṇā iti praiṣaḥ |
7.2.d: होता यक्षन् मित्रा वरुणा इति प्रैषः ।
7.2.m: ‘Let the Hotṛ worship Mitra and Varuṇa’ is the ritual summons.
‘Praised by Jamadagni’ is the consecratory verse.
‘Yoked at dawn’ is the introductory verse for the cup for the Aśvins.
‘Let the Hotṛ worship the two Aśvins’ is the ritual summons.

7.2.s: anavānam dvidevatyānām puronuvākyāḥ praiṣāṃś ca āha |
7.2.d: अनवानम् द्विदेवत्यानाम् पुरोनुवाक्याः प्रैषांश् च आह ।
7.2.m: He recites the introductory verses and the ritual summonses of the two-deity cups without taking breath.
The two introductory verses of the cup for Indra-Vāyu have separate praṇavas.

7.2.s: sakṛt purastāj japo ye yajāmaho anumantraṇaś ca |
7.2.d: सकृत् पुरस्ताज् जपो ये यजामहो अनुमन्त्रणश् च ।
7.2.m: The whispering beforehand, the ye yajāmahe, and the following recitation are done once.

7.3.s: etu vasuḥ purūvasur ity aindravāyavam pratigṛhya urau dakṣiṇe nidhāya anapidhānam anavekṣaṇam ca dvidevatyānām ā śeṣasya avanayanāt |
7.3.d: एतु वसुः पुरूवसुर् इत्य् ऐन्द्रवायवम् प्रतिगृह्य उरौ दक्षिणे निधाय अनपिधानम् अनवेक्षणम् च द्विदेवत्यानाम् आ शेषस्य अवनयनात् ।
7.3.m: Having accepted the cup for Indra-Vāyu with ‘May Vasu, rich in wealth, come’, and placed it on his right thigh, there is no covering and no looking at the two-deity cups until the pouring in of the residue.

7.3.s: etu vasur vidad vasur iti maitrāvaruṇam pratigṛhya dakṣiṇena aindravāyavam hṛtvā dakṣiṇataḥ paścān nidadhāti |
7.3.d: एतु वसुर् विदद् वसुर् इति मैत्रावरुणम् प्रतिगृह्य दक्षिणेन ऐन्द्रवायवम् हृत्वा दक्षिणतः पश्चान् निदधाति ।
7.3.m: Having accepted the cup for Mitra-Varuṇa with ‘May Vasu, finding wealth, come’, and brought it past the cup for Indra-Vāyu to the right, he places it to the south, behind.

7.3.s: aitu vasuḥ samyad vasur ity āśvinam pratigṛhya dakṣiṇena pūrvau hṛtvā uttarataḥ paścān nidadhāti |
7.3.d: ऐतु वसुः सम्यद् वसुर् इत्य् आश्विनम् प्रतिगृह्य दक्षिणेन पूर्वौ हृत्वा उत्तरतः पश्चान् निदधाति ।
7.3.m: Having accepted the cup for the Aśvins with ‘May Vasu, gathering wealth, come’, and brought it past the previous two to the right, he places it to the north, behind.

7.3.s: somasya agne vīhi ity anuvaṣaṭ kāraḥ sarvāsu soma yājyāsu dvidevatya ṛtu yājān parhāpya āditya graha sāvitra grahau pātnīvatam ca |
7.3.d: सोमस्य अग्ने वीहि इत्य् अनुवषट् कारः सर्वासु सोम याज्यासु द्विदेवत्य ऋतु याजान् पर्हाप्य आदित्य ग्रह सावित्र ग्रहौ पात्नीवतम् च ।
7.3.m: ‘O Agni, enjoy the soma’ is the secondary vaṣaṭ-call in all consecratory verses for soma, except for the two-deity offerings and the seasonal offerings, the cup for Āditya, the cup for Savitṛ, and that for the wives of the gods.
Or, in a low voice in that for the wives of the gods.

7.4.s: unnīyamānebhya ity ukta ā tvā vahantu haraya ity unnīyamāna sūktam |
7.4.d: उन्नीयमानेभ्य इत्य् उक्त आ त्वा वहन्तु हरय इत्य् उन्नीयमान सूक्तम् ।
7.4.m: When ‘For those being drawn up’ has been said, the hymn for the being drawn up is ‘May the bay horses bring you here’.

7.4.s: hotā yakṣad indram prātaḥ prātaḥ sāvasya iti praiṣaḥ |
7.4.d: होता यक्षद् इन्द्रम् प्रातः प्रातः सावस्य इति प्रैषः ।
7.4.m: ‘Let the Hotṛ worship Indra of the morning pressing’ is the ritual summons.

7.4.s: idam te somyam madhv iti yajati |
7.4.d: इदम् ते सोम्यम् मध्व् इति यजति ।
7.4.m: He recites the offering verse with ‘This is your somic honey’.

7.4.s: nṛ cakṣasam tvā nṛ cakṣāḥ pratīkṣa iti hotṛ camasam pratīkṣya vayodhasam tvā vayodhāḥ pratigṛhṇāmi iti pratigṛhya uraḥ saṃsparśayati dvidevatyāṃś ca |
7.4.d: नृ चक्षसम् त्वा नृ चक्षाः प्रतीक्ष इति होतृ चमसम् प्रतीक्ष्य वयोधसम् त्वा वयोधाः प्रतिगृह्णामि इति प्रतिगृह्य उरः संस्पर्शयति द्विदेवत्यांश् च ।
7.4.m: Having looked at the Hotṛ's cup with ‘Looking upon men, I look upon you who look upon men’, and accepted it with ‘Possessing vitality, I accept you who possess vitality’, he touches his chest [with it], and [so also with] the two-deity cups.
The Hotrakas recite the offering verses for the [cups] drawn up again.

7.4.s: indra tvā vṛṣabham iti brāhmaṇa ācchaṃsī |
7.4.d: इन्द्र त्वा वृषभम् इति ब्राह्मण आच्छंसी ।
7.4.m: The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with ‘Indra, you the bull’.
The Āgnīdhra with ‘To him who has oxen for food’.

7.4.s: ayāḷ agnīd ity ukte ayāḷ ity āgnīdhraḥ |
7.4.d: अयाऌ अग्नीद् इत्य् उक्ते अयाऌ इत्य् आग्नीध्रः ।
7.4.m: When ‘The Āgnīdh has sacrificed’ is said, the Āgnīdhra says ‘He has sacrificed’.

7.4.s: sa bhadram akar yo naḥ somam pāyayiṣyati iti hotā |
7.4.d: स भद्रम् अकर् यो नः सोमम् पाययिष्यति इति होता ।
7.4.m: The Hotṛ says, ‘He has done well, who will make us drink soma’.

7.4.s: somam bhakṣayiṣyanto yājñikair nāma dheyair asā upahvayasva iti kartāro anyo anyasminn upahavam icchante |
7.4.d: सोमम् भक्षयिष्यन्तो याज्ञिकैर् नाम धेयैर् असा उपह्वयस्व इति कर्तारो अन्यो अन्यस्मिन्न् उपहवम् इच्छन्ते ।
7.4.m: About to consume the soma, the officiants, using sacrificial names, seek invitation from one another with ‘O so-and-so, invite [me]’.
The maker of the vaṣaṭ consumes first.

7.4.s: pratibhakṣitam dvidevatya śeṣam nārāśaṃsavatām ca grahāṇām hotṛ camase avanayati hute tvā bhakṣitam avanayāmy ūrjasvantam devebhya āyuṣmantam mahyam iti |
7.4.d: प्रतिभक्षितम् द्विदेवत्य शेषम् नाराशंसवताम् च ग्रहाणाम् होतृ चमसे अवनयति हुते त्वा भक्षितम् अवनयाम्य् ऊर्जस्वन्तम् देवेभ्य आयुष्मन्तम् मह्यम् इति ।
7.4.m: He pours the residue of the consumed two-deity cups and of the cups accompanied by Nārāśaṃsa into the Hotṛ's cup with: ‘Offered, consumed, I pour you in, full of vigor for the gods, full of life for me’.

7.4.s: dvir aindra vāyava śeṣasya avanayanam tatra abhyāvartate mantraḥ |
7.4.d: द्विर् ऐन्द्र वायव शेषस्य अवनयनम् तत्र अभ्यावर्तते मन्त्रः ।
7.4.m: Twice is the pouring in of the residue of the cup for Indra-Vāyu; in that case the mantra is repeated.

7.4.s: anavasarjanam ca dvidevatyānām ā śeṣasya avanayanāt |
7.4.d: अनवसर्जनम् च द्विदेवत्यानाम् आ शेषस्य अवनयनात् ।
7.4.m: And there is no letting go of the two-deity cups until the pouring in of the residue.

7.5.s: iha vasuḥ purūvasur ity aindra vāyavam adhvaryave pragṛhya upahūtau vāyur indra vāyū saha prāṇena saha varcasā tayor aham upahūtaḥ saha prāṇena saha varcasā iti bhakṣayitvā pragrahaṇa mantreṇa punaḥ pragṛhya bhakṣa mantreṇa punar bhakṣayati |
7.5.d: इह वसुः पुरूवसुर् इत्य् ऐन्द्र वायवम् अध्वर्यवे प्रगृह्य उपहूतौ वायुर् इन्द्र वायू सह प्राणेन सह वर्चसा तयोर् अहम् उपहूतः सह प्राणेन सह वर्चसा इति भक्षयित्वा प्रग्रहण मन्त्रेण पुनः प्रगृह्य भक्ष मन्त्रेण पुनर् भक्षयति ।
7.5.m: Having held forward the cup for Indra-Vāyu to the Adhvaryu with ‘Here is Vasu, rich in wealth’, and having consumed it with ‘Vāyu and Indra-Vāyu are invited together with breath, together with vigor; invited by them two am I together with breath, together with vigor’, having held it forward again with the holding-forward mantra, he consumes it again with the consumption mantra.

7.5.s: iha vasur vidad vasur iti maitrāvaruṇam pragṛhya |
7.5.d: इह वसुर् विदद् वसुर् इति मैत्रावरुणम् प्रगृह्य ।
7.5.m: Having held forward the cup for Mitra-Varuṇa with ‘Here is Vasu, finding wealth’,

7.5.s: upahūtau mitrāvaruṇau saha cakṣuṣā saha varcasā tayor aham upahūtaḥ saha cakṣuṣā saha varcasā iti bhakṣayitvā |
7.5.d: उपहूतौ मित्रावरुणौ सह चक्षुषा सह वर्चसा तयोर् अहम् उपहूतः सह चक्षुषा सह वर्चसा इति भक्षयित्वा ।
7.5.m: and having consumed it with ‘Mitra and Varuṇa are invited together with sight, together with vigor; invited by them two am I together with sight, together with vigor’,

7.5.s: āśvinam pradakṣiṇam śiraḥ paryāhṛtya avekṣya pratiparyāhṛtya avekṣya |
7.5.d: आश्विनम् प्रदक्षिणम् शिरः पर्याहृत्य अवेक्ष्य प्रतिपर्याहृत्य अवेक्ष्य ।
7.5.m: having moved the cup for the Aśvins around clockwise past his head and looked at it, and having moved it back around and looked at it,

7.5.s: iha vasuḥ samyad vasur ity āśvinam pragṛhya |
7.5.d: इह वसुः सम्यद् वसुर् इत्य् आश्विनम् प्रगृह्य ।
7.5.m: having held forward the cup for the Aśvins with ‘Here is Vasu, gathering wealth’,

7.5.s: upahūtau devāv aśvinau saha śrotreṇa saha varcasā tayor aham upahūtaḥ saha śrotreṇa saha varcasā iti bhakṣayitvā |
7.5.d: उपहूतौ देवाव् अश्विनौ सह श्रोत्रेण सह वर्चसा तयोर् अहम् उपहूतः सह श्रोत्रेण सह वर्चसा इति भक्षयित्वा ।
7.5.m: and having consumed it with ‘The divine Aśvins are invited together with hearing, together with vigor; invited by them two am I together with hearing, together with vigor’,

7.5.s: upaspṛśya iḷām upahvayate |
7.5.d: उपस्पृश्य इऌआम् उपह्वयते ।
7.5.m: having touched water, he invokes the Iḷā.

7.5.s: upodyacchanti camasān |
7.5.d: उपोद्यच्छन्ति चमसान् ।
7.5.m: They lift up the cups.

7.5.s: hotṛ camasam anvārabhate |
7.5.d: होतृ चमसम् अन्वारभते ।
7.5.m: He touches the Hotṛ's cup from behind.

7.5.s: asaṃsparśanam sarvatra ājya lepena somasya |
7.5.d: असंस्पर्शनम् सर्वत्र आज्य लेपेन सोमस्य ।
7.5.m: Everywhere there must be no contact of the soma with the smear of clarified butter.

7.5.s: upahūya prasthitā bhakṣayanti |
7.5.d: उपहूय प्रस्थिता भक्षयन्ति ।
7.5.m: Having invited [one another], they consume the drawn portions.

7.5.s: tejase tvā brahma varcasāya bhakṣayāmi iti bhakṣa mantraḥ prātaḥ savane |
7.5.d: तेजसे त्वा ब्रह्म वर्चसाय भक्षयामि इति भक्ष मन्त्रः प्रातः सवने ।
7.5.m: ‘For fiery energy, for brahmanic luster, I consume you’ is the consumption mantra at the morning pressing.

7.5.s: ojase tvā indriyāya bhakṣayāmi iti mādhyaṃdine |
7.5.d: ओजसे त्वा इन्द्रियाय भक्षयामि इति माध्यंदिने ।
7.5.m: ‘For vigor, for faculty power, I consume you’ at the midday [pressing].

7.5.s: prajāyai tvā puṣṭyai bhakṣayāmi iti tṛtīya savane |
7.5.d: प्रजायै त्वा पुष्ट्यै भक्षयामि इति तृतीय सवने ।
7.5.m: "For offspring, for nourishment I consume you" is [the formula] at the third pressing.

7.5.s: śam no bhava hṛda ity uro abhimarśanī bhakṣayitvā |
7.5.d: शम् नो भव हृद इत्य् उरो अभिमर्शनी भक्षयित्वा ।
7.5.m: Having consumed [it], the verse touching the chest is: "Be auspicious to our heart..."

7.5.s: savye pāṇau camasān kṛtvā dakṣiṇena āpyāyayanti |
7.5.d: सव्ये पाणौ चमसान् कृत्वा दक्षिणेन आप्याययन्ति ।
7.5.m: Placing the cups in their left hands, they swell [the Soma] with their right.

7.5.s: ā pyāyasva sametu tu ity āpyāyanī prātaḥ savane |
7.5.d: आ प्यायस्व समेतु तु इत्य् आप्यायनी प्रातः सवने ।
7.5.m: "Swell up, let gather..." is the swelling verse at the morning pressing;

7.5.s: sam te payāṃsi ity uttarayoḥ |
7.5.d: सम् ते पयांसि इत्य् उत्तरयोः ।
7.5.m: "Let your juices gather..." at the latter two [pressings].

7.5.s: prasthitān āpyāyayanti |
7.5.d: प्रस्थितान् आप्याययन्ति ।
7.5.m: They swell the [cups of] the set-forth offerings.

7.5.s: ājye marutvatīye ca |
7.5.d: आज्ये मरुत्वतीये च ।

7.5.s: ājya praugayor nārāśaṃsā niṣkevalya marutvatīyayor vaiśvadeve ca |
7.5.d: आज्य प्रौगयोर् नाराशंसा निष्केवल्य मरुत्वतीययोर् वैश्वदेवे च ।
7.5.m: The Nārāśaṃsa [cups are consumed] at the ājya and prauga [śastras], at the niṣkevalya and marutvatīya [śastras], and at the vaiśvadeva [śastra].

7.5.s: devo asi narāśaṃso yat te medhaḥ svar jyotis tasya ta ūmaiḥ pitṛbhir bhakṣitasya upahūtasya upahūto bhakṣayāmi iti bhakṣa mantraḥ prātaḥ savane nārāśaṃsānām |
7.5.d: देवो असि नराशंसो यत् ते मेधः स्वर् ज्योतिस् तस्य त ऊमैः पितृभिर् भक्षितस्य उपहूतस्य उपहूतो भक्षयामि इति भक्ष मन्त्रः प्रातः सवने नाराशंसानाम् ।
7.5.m: "A god are you, Narāśaṃsa; what sap of yours is heaven's light, of that belonging to you, consumed by the Ūma ancestors, invited by the invited one, I consume" is the consuming formula for the Nārāśaṃsa [cups] at the morning pressing.

7.5.s: ūrvair iti mādhyaṃdine vikāraḥ |
7.5.d: ऊर्वैर् इति माध्यंदिने विकारः ।
7.5.m: "By the Ūrva [ancestors]" is the modification at the midday [pressing];

7.5.s: kāvyair iti tṛtīya savane |
7.5.d: काव्यैर् इति तृतीय सवने ।
7.5.m: "By the Kāvya [ancestors]" at the third pressing.

7.6.s: acchāvākaḥ sīda ity ukto agreṇa sada uttareṇa srutim upaviśya puroḷāśam pratigṛhya acchāvāka vadasva ity ukto acchā vo agnim avasa iti tisro anvāha |
7.6.d: अच्छावाकः सीद इत्य् उक्तो अग्रेण सद उत्तरेण स्रुतिम् उपविश्य पुरोऌआशम् प्रतिगृह्य अच्छावाक वदस्व इत्य् उक्तो अच्छा वो अग्निम् अवस इति तिस्रो अन्वाह ।
7.6.m: When told, "Acchāvāka, sit down," having sat down in front of the sadas north of the path, having accepted the sacrificial cake, and having been told, "Acchāvāka, speak," he recites three [verses beginning]: "Towards your Agni for help..."

7.6.s: yajamāna hotar adhvaryo agnīd brahman potar neṣṭar uta upavaktar iṣeṣayadhvam ūrjor jayadhvam ni vo jāmayo jihatām ny ajāmayo ni sapatnā yāmani bādhitāso jeṣatha abhītvarīm jeṣatha abhītvaryāḥ śravad va indraḥ śṛṇavad vo agniḥ prasthāya indra agnibhyām somam vocata upo asmān brāhmaṇān brāhmaṇā hvayadhvam iti |
7.6.d: यजमान होतर् अध्वर्यो अग्नीद् ब्रह्मन् पोतर् नेष्टर् उत उपवक्तर् इषेषयध्वम् ऊर्जोर् जयध्वम् नि वो जामयो जिहताम् न्य् अजामयो नि सपत्ना यामनि बाधितासो जेषथ अभीत्वरीम् जेषथ अभीत्वर्याः श्रवद् व इन्द्रः शृणवद् वो अग्निः प्रस्थाय इन्द्र अग्निभ्याम् सोमम् वोचत उपो अस्मान् ब्राह्मणान् ब्राह्मणा ह्वयध्वम् इति ।
7.6.m: "O Sacrificer, Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Āgnīdhra, Brahman, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Upavaktṛ! Strive for refreshment, conquer with vigor! Let your kinsmen bow low, let non-kinsmen [bow low], low [bow] rivals defeated on their course! May you conquer the advancing [foe]! May you conquer the advancing [forces]! May Indra hear you, may Agni listen to you! Having set forth, speak the Soma for Indra and Agni! Invite us, [who are] brahmins, O brahmins!"

7.6.s: upahavam ayam brāhmaṇa icchate acchāvāko vā ity adhvaryur āha tam hotar upahvayasva iti |
7.6.d: उपहवम् अयम् ब्राह्मण इच्छते अच्छावाको वा इत्य् अध्वर्युर् आह तम् होतर् उपह्वयस्व इति ।
7.6.m: The Adhvaryu says: "This brahmin desires invitation, or [is it] the Acchāvāka? Invite him, O Hotṛ!"

7.6.s: pratyetā vāmā sūktāyam sunvan yajamāno agrabhīd uta pratiṣṭhotā upavakta uta no gāva upahūtā uta upahūta ity upahvāsyamānaḥ |
7.6.d: प्रत्येता वामा सूक्तायम् सुन्वन् यजमानो अग्रभीद् उत प्रतिष्ठोता उपवक्त उत नो गाव उपहूता उत उपहूत इत्य् उपह्वास्यमानः ।
7.6.m:
When he intends to invite [him, he recites]: "The receiver of desirable things, in this hymn, the pressing sacrificer has grasped, and the support, the Hotṛ, the Upavaktṛ; and our cattle are invited, and [you are] invited."

When he does not intend to invite [him, he stops] up to: "And our cattle are invited."

7.6.s: uta no gāva upahūtā ity āto anupahvāsyamānaḥ |
7.6.d: उत नो गाव उपहूता इत्य् आतो अनुपह्वास्यमानः ।

7.6.s: anupahūto acchāvāko nivartadhvam iti sūktasya yāvat śaknuyāt tāvad anudravet |
7.6.d: अनुपहूतो अच्छावाको निवर्तध्वम् इति सूक्तस्य यावत् शक्नुयात् तावद् अनुद्रवेत् ।
7.6.m: If uninvited, the Acchāvāka should run through as much as he can of the hymn [beginning]: "Turn back..."
Or the Hotṛ, having mutually invited the Acchāvāka who desires it,

7.7.s: unnīyamānāya ity uktaḥ praty asmai pipīṣata ity acchāvākaḥ sūtram anvāha |
7.7.d: उन्नीयमानाय इत्य् उक्तः प्रत्य् अस्मै पिपीषत इत्य् अच्छावाकः सूत्रम् अन्वाह ।
7.7.m: being told, "For the one being drawn up," the Acchāvāka recites the hymn [beginning]: "To this one who desires to drink..."
He recites the offering verse [beginning]: "With the early travelers..."

7.7.s: bhakṣitā āpyāyitam camasam adhvaryave pradāya dakṣiṇa āvṛd aparayā dvārā sadaḥ prapadya svasya dhiṣṇyasya paścād upaviśya puroḷāśam prāśnāti |
7.7.d: भक्षिता आप्यायितम् चमसम् अध्वर्यवे प्रदाय दक्षिण आवृद् अपरया द्वारा सदः प्रपद्य स्वस्य धिष्ण्यस्य पश्चाद् उपविश्य पुरोऌआशम् प्राश्नाति ।
7.7.m: Having handed the cup, consumed and swollen, to the Adhvaryu, turning to the right, having entered the sadas by the western door, and having sat down behind his own dhiṣṇya hearth, he eats the sacrificial cake.

7.7.s: pūrvaḥ prasṛptaś ced acchāvākīyām kuryāt svena visaṃsthita saṃcareṇa niṣkramya acchāvākasya bahiṣ karma kṛtvā sva karma kurute |
7.7.d: पूर्वः प्रसृप्तश् चेद् अच्छावाकीयाम् कुर्यात् स्वेन विसंस्थित संचरेण निष्क्रम्य अच्छावाकस्य बहिष् कर्म कृत्वा स्व कर्म कुरुते ।
7.7.m: If he had crept in beforehand, he should perform the Acchāvāka's duty; having gone out by his own regular path of movement during the non-concluded [rites] and performed the Acchāvāka's external duty, he performs his own duty.
There is an option regarding the consecratory verses of the assistant Hotṛ priests:

7.7.s: prātaḥ savane anvāananto yajanty ardharcaśo vā |
7.7.d: प्रातः सवने अन्वाअनन्तो यजन्त्य् अर्धर्चशो वा ।
7.7.m: At the morning pressing, they recite the offering verses without drawing breath, or by half-verses.

7.8.m: Then they proceed with the seasonal offerings.

7.8.s: hotā yakṣad indrma hotrād ity ṛtu praiṣair anavānam preṣyati |
7.8.d: होता यक्षद् इन्द्र्म होत्राद् इत्य् ऋतु प्रैषैर् अनवानम् प्रेष्यति ।
7.8.m: He issues the ritual summons without drawing breath with the seasonal summonses [beginning]: "May the Hotṛ worship Indra from the Hotṛ's cup..."

7.8.s: yena preṣyati sā yājyā uddhṛtya hotā ayakṣam asau yajam ca |
7.8.d: येन प्रेष्यति सा याज्या उद्धृत्य होता अयक्षम् असौ यजम् च ।
7.8.m: That with which he issues the summons is the consecratory verse, having omitted: "May the Hotṛ worship..." and "...worship this one!"

7.8.s: maidhātithyo vā indra somam piba ṛtunā iti |
7.8.d: मैधातिथ्यो वा इन्द्र सोमम् पिब ऋतुना इति ।
7.8.m: Or the verse of Medhātithi: "O Indra, drink Soma in due season..."

7.8.s: yo yaḥ praiṣa ante śrūyate sa sa yajati |
7.8.d: यो यः प्रैष अन्ते श्रूयते स स यजति ।
7.8.m: Whichever [priest] is heard at the end of the ritual summons, he recites the offering verse.

7.8.s: hotar etad yaja ity adhvaryur āha |
7.8.d: होतर् एतद् यज इत्य् अध्वर्युर् आह ।
7.8.m: The Adhvaryu says: "Hotṛ, recite the offering verse for this!"
They consume [the cups] in the order in which the vaṣaṭ-call was made.

7.8.s: limped iva eva jighred atra dvidevatyeṣu ca iti |
7.8.d: लिम्पेद् इव एव जिघ्रेद् अत्र द्विदेवत्येषु च इति ।
7.8.m: He should merely smear [his lips], as it were, [or] sniff here and at the two-deity cups.

7.9.s: ājyam śaṃsiṣyan pitā mātariśvā acchidrā pada uśig asīyān utakṣiṣat somo nīthavin nīthāni neṣad bṛhaspatir ukthāmadāni śaṃsiṣad iti japitvā śoṃsāvo ity āhāvaḥ śastra ādau prātaḥ savane tena āhūya upāṃśu tūṣṇīm śaṃsam |
7.9.d: आज्यम् शंसिष्यन् पिता मातरिश्वा अच्छिद्रा पद उशिग् असीयान् उतक्षिषत् सोमो नीथविन् नीथानि नेषद् बृहस्पतिर् उक्थामदानि शंसिषद् इति जपित्वा शोंसावो इत्य् आहावः शस्त्र आदौ प्रातः सवने तेन आहूय उपांशु तूष्णीम् शंसम् ।
7.9.m: Intending to recite the ājya-śastra, having muttered: "Father Mātariśvan, may the unerring foot, desiring, carve out a better [path]; may Soma, knowing the guidance, lead the guides; may Bṛhaspati recite the uktha-gladdening verses," the call at the beginning of a śastra at the morning pressing is: "Let us two recite!"; having called with this, [he recites] the silent praise in a low voice:

7.9.s: agnir jyotir jyotir agnir ity avasāya indro jyotir jyotir indra ity avasāya sūryo jyotir jyotiḥ sūrya ity avasāya paccho avasyan purorucam |
7.9.d: अग्निर् ज्योतिर् ज्योतिर् अग्निर् इत्य् अवसाय इन्द्रो ज्योतिर् ज्योतिर् इन्द्र इत्य् अवसाय सूर्यो ज्योतिर् ज्योतिः सूर्य इत्य् अवसाय पच्छो अवस्यन् पुरोरुचम् ।
7.9.m: Having paused at "Agni is light, light is Agni," having paused at "Indra is light, light is Indra," having paused at "Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya," pausing by verse-quarters, [he recites] the introductory invocation:

7.9.s: agnir deva iddhaḥ | agnir manv iddhaḥ | rathīr adhvarāṇāmṇ | atūrto hotā | tūrṇir havyavāṭ | ā devo devān vakṣat | yakṣad agnir devo devān | so adhvarā karati jāta vedo pra vo devāya ity ājyam |
7.9.d: अग्निर् देव इद्धः । अग्निर् मन्व् इद्धः । रथीर् अध्वराणाम्ण् । अतूर्तो होता । तूर्णिर् हव्यवाट् । आ देवो देवान् वक्षत् । यक्षद् अग्निर् देवो देवान् । सो अध्वरा करति जात वेदो प्र वो देवाय इत्य् आज्यम् ।
7.9.m: "Agni kindled by the gods / Agni kindled by Manu / charioteer of the sacrifices / unhindered Hotṛ / swift conveyer of oblations / may the god bring the gods hither / may Agni the god sacrifice to the gods / he shall perform the rites, knowing all beings / Forth to your god..." is the ājya-śastra.
Its first half-verse is recited without drawing breath, verse-quarter by verse-quarter.
And [likewise] at the marutvatīya and vaiśvadeva [śastras].

7.9.s: sūkta śeṣam śastvā āhūya uttamayā paridhāya uktha vīryam japati bhā vibhā uṣāḥ svar jyotiḥ ślokāya tvā uktham avāci iti |
7.9.d: सूक्त शेषम् शस्त्वा आहूय उत्तमया परिधाय उक्थ वीर्यम् जपति भा विभा उषाः स्वर् ज्योतिः श्लोकाय त्वा उक्थम् अवाचि इति ।
7.9.m: Having recited the remainder of the hymn, having called, having concluded with the final verse, he mutters the essence of the uktha: "Light, radiance, dawn, heaven's light; for praise to you the uktha has been spoken."

7.9.s: ukthaśā ity adhvaryur āha sarvāsu śastra yājyāsu |
7.9.d: उक्थशा इत्य् अध्वर्युर् आह सर्वासु शस्त्र याज्यासु ।
7.9.m: The Adhvaryu says: "Reciter of the uktha!" in all the śastra consecratory verses.
He recites the offering verse [beginning]: "O Agni and Indra..."

7.10.m: When the ājya-śastra is completed, they chant the stotra.

7.10.s: stotravatām śastrāṇām eṣā iti prāha uttamāt pratīhārād ūrdhvam āhūya śaṃsanti |
7.10.d: स्तोत्रवताम् शस्त्राणाम् एषा इति प्राह उत्तमात् प्रतीहाराद् ऊर्ध्वम् आहूय शंसन्ति ।
7.10.m: "This is [the rule] for the śastras that possess stotras," he declares; having called after the final pratīhāra, they recite.

7.10.s: prauge antareṇa mādhucchandasāṃs tṛcān ṛco vyavayanti tāḥ puroruca ity ācakṣate |
7.10.d: प्रौगे अन्तरेण माधुच्छन्दसांस् तृचान् ऋचो व्यवयन्ति ताः पुरोरुच इत्य् आचक्षते ।
7.10.m: In the Prauga-śastra, between the triplets composed by Madhucchandas, they interweave verses; these they call puroruc verses.

7.10.s: tasyām dvābhyām dvābhyām avasāya dvābhyām praṇauti |
7.10.d: तस्याम् द्वाभ्याम् द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय द्वाभ्याम् प्रणौति ।
7.10.m: In it, having paused after every two lines, he pronounces the praṇava after every two lines.

7.10.s: sārasvatyām vikalpaḥ | śaṃsen na vā | nityas tv āhāvaḥ |
7.10.d: सारस्वत्याम् विकल्पः । शंसेन् न वा । नित्यस् त्व् आहावः ।
7.10.m: In the verse to Sarasvatī there is an option: he may recite it, or not; but the call is constant.

7.10.s: vāyur agregā yajñaprīḥ sākam gan manasā yajñam | śivo niyudbhiḥ śivābhiḥ | iti sakṛt śastvā vāyav ā yāhi darśata iti tisṛṇām triḥ prathamām |
7.10.d: वायुर् अग्रेगा यज्ञप्रीः साकम् गन् मनसा यज्ञम् । शिवो नियुद्भिः शिवाभिः । इति सकृत् शस्त्वा वायव् आ याहि दर्शत इति तिसृणाम् त्रिः प्रथमाम् ।
7.10.m: "Vāyu, going in front, delighting in sacrifice, has come together in mind to the sacrifice / auspicious with his auspicious teams /" having recited [this] once, [he recites] three times the first of the three verses [beginning]: "O Vāyu, come, visible..."

7.10.s: hiraṇya vartanī narā devā patī abhiṣṭaye | vāyuś ca indraś ca sumakhau | indra vāyū ima iti tisraḥ |
7.10.d: हिरण्य वर्तनी नरा देवा पती अभिष्टये । वायुश् च इन्द्रश् च सुमखौ । इन्द्र वायू इम इति तिस्रः ।
7.10.m: "Following a golden course, hero gods, lords, for assistance / and Vāyu and Indra, noble champions /" [then] the three verses [beginning]: "O Indra and Vāyu, these [somas]..."

7.10.s: kāvyayor ājāneṣu kratvā dakṣasya duroṇe | riśādasā sadhasya ā | mitram huva iti tisraḥ |
7.10.d: काव्ययोर् आजानेषु क्रत्वा दक्षस्य दुरोणे । रिशादसा सधस्य आ । मित्रम् हुव इति तिस्रः ।
7.10.m: "In the births of the two kinsmen through insight, in the home of Dakṣa, the two consumers of the foe in the assembly"; "I call upon Mitra"—[these] three.

7.10.s: daivyāv adhvaryū ā gatam rathena sūrya tvacā | madhvā yajñam samañjāthe | aśvinā yajvarīr iṣa iti tisraḥ |
7.10.d: दैव्याव् अध्वर्यू आ गतम् रथेन सूर्य त्वचा । मध्वा यज्ञम् समञ्जाथे । अश्विना यज्वरीर् इष इति तिस्रः ।
7.10.m: "O two divine Adhvaryus, come with your chariot with sun-like skin; you anoint the sacrifice with sweet drink"; "O Aśvins, the sacrificing refreshments"—[these] three.

7.10.s: indra ukthebhir bhiandiṣṭho vājānām ca vāja patiḥ | harivān sutānām sakhā | indrā yāhi citra bhāno iti tisraḥ |
7.10.d: इन्द्र उक्थेभिर् भिअन्दिष्ठो वाजानाम् च वाज पतिः । हरिवान् सुतानाम् सखा । इन्द्रा याहि चित्र भानो इति तिस्रः ।
7.10.m: "Indra, most generous through praises and lord of refreshments of refreshments, possessing bay horses, the friend of the pressed [drinks]"; "Come, Indra, of radiant light"—[these] three.

7.10.s: viśvān devān havāmahe asmin yajñe sajoṣasaḥ | ta imam yajñam āgaman devāso devyo dhiyā | ye yajñasya tanū kṛto viśva ā soma pītaye | omāsaś carṣaṇīdhṛta iti tisraḥ |
7.10.d: विश्वान् देवान् हवामहे अस्मिन् यज्ञे सजोषसः । त इमम् यज्ञम् आगमन् देवासो देव्यो धिया । ये यज्ञस्य तनू कृतो विश्व आ सोम पीतये । ओमासश् चर्षणीधृत इति तिस्रः ।
7.10.m: "We invoke all the gods, united at this sacrifice; may those gods, divine with thought, come to this sacrifice; who are the makers of the body of the sacrifice, all to drink the Soma"; "O protectors, upholders of men"—[these] three.

7.10.s: vācām aham devīm vācam asmin yajñe supeśasam | sarasvatīm havāmahe | pāvakā naḥ sarasvatī iti tisṛṇām uttamayā paridhāya uktha vīryam japati vācam me jinva | prāṇam me tṛmpa | cakṣur me pāhi | śrotram me ava | varṇam me yaccha | tanvam me pāhi | yaśo me dhehi | ghoṣāya tvā uktham avāci iti |
7.10.d: वाचाम् अहम् देवीम् वाचम् अस्मिन् यज्ञे सुपेशसम् । सरस्वतीम् हवामहे । पावका नः सरस्वती इति तिसृणाम् उत्तमया परिधाय उक्थ वीर्यम् जपति वाचम् मे जिन्व । प्राणम् मे तृम्प । चक्षुर् मे पाहि । श्रोत्रम् मे अव । वर्णम् मे यच्छ । तन्वम् मे पाहि । यशो मे धेहि । घोषाय त्वा उक्थम् अवाचि इति ।
7.10.m: "We invoke the goddess of speeches, Speech, well-adorned at this sacrifice, Sarasvatī"; having concluded [the Prauga-śastra] with the last of the three [verses beginning] "May Sarasvatī, purifying us", he murmurs the power of the hymn: "Quicken my speech; satisfy my breath; protect my sight; preserve my hearing; bestow color on me; protect my body; place glory in me; for sound the hymn has been spoken to you."
He recites the offering verse: "With all [the gods], the Soma-drink, the sweet drink".

7.11.m: The strophe and antistrophe verses are triplets, leaving aside the pragāthas.

7.11.s: ā no mitā varuṇā no gantam iti stotriya anurūpau maitrāvaruṇasya |
7.11.d: आ नो मिता वरुणा नो गन्तम् इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ मैत्रावरुणस्य ।
7.11.m: "Come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa" are the strophe and antistrophe of the Maitrāvaruṇa.

7.11.s: pra vo mitrāya ity uktha mukham |
7.11.d: प्र वो मित्राय इत्य् उक्थ मुखम् ।
7.11.m: "Forth to your Mitra" is the opening of the hymn.

7.11.s: pra mitrayor iti navānām uttamayā paridhāya upa naḥ sutamā gatam iti yajati |
7.11.d: प्र मित्रयोर् इति नवानाम् उत्तमया परिधाय उप नः सुतमा गतम् इति यजति ।
7.11.m: Having concluded with the last of the nine [verses beginning] "Forth of the two, Mitra [and Varuṇa]", he recites the offering verse: "Come to our pressed [drink]".

7.12.s: ā yāhi suṣuma iti brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaḥ stotriya anurūpau |
7.12.d: आ याहि सुषुम इति ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ ।
7.12.m: "Come, we have pressed" are the strophe and antistrophe of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

7.12.s: śeṣaḥ sūktasya uktha mukham uttame parihāpya |
7.12.d: शेषः सूक्तस्य उक्थ मुखम् उत्तमे परिहाप्य ।
7.12.m: The remainder of the hymn is the opening of the hymn, leaving aside the last two [verses].

7.12.s: ud ghed abhi iti tisṛṇām uttamayā paridhāya indra kratuvidam iti yajati |
7.12.d: उद् घेद् अभि इति तिसृणाम् उत्तमया परिधाय इन्द्र क्रतुविदम् इति यजति ।
7.12.m: Having concluded with the last of the three [verses beginning] "Up indeed...", he recites the offering verse: "Indra, the finder of wisdom".

7.13.s: indra agnī ā gatam sutam ity acchāvākasya stotriya anurūpau |
7.13.d: इन्द्र अग्नी आ गतम् सुतम् इत्य् अच्छावाकस्य स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ ।
7.13.m: "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [drink]" are the strophe and antistrophe of the Acchāvāka.
The remainder of the hymn is the opening of the hymn.

7.13.s: iha indra agnī upa hvaya iti pañca |
7.13.d: इह इन्द्र अग्नी उप ह्वय इति पञ्च ।
7.13.m: "Here, O Indra and Agni, call upon" are five [verses].

7.13.s: iyam vāmasya manmana iti navānām uttamayā paridhāya indra agnī ā gatam sutam iti yajati |
7.13.d: इयम् वामस्य मन्मन इति नवानाम् उत्तमया परिधाय इन्द्र अग्नी आ गतम् सुतम् इति यजति ।
7.13.m: Having concluded with the last of the nine [verses beginning] "This prayer of this [singer] for you two", he recites the offering verse: "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed [drink]".

7.14.s: mitram vayam indram id gāthina indra agna iti stotriyā bṛhat pṛṣṭhasya |
7.14.d: मित्रम् वयम् इन्द्रम् इद् गाथिन इन्द्र अग्न इति स्तोत्रिया बृहत् पृष्ठस्य ।
7.14.m: "Mitra we...", "Indra alone, the singers...", and "O Indra and Agni..." are the strophe verses of the Bṛhat chant pṛṣṭha-stotra.
The Acchāvāka makes the Rathantara [verse] the strophe [and] antistrophe.
And the Hotṛ [also does so] in the additional hymns.

7.14.s: stotriya anurūpābhyām yac ca anantaram anurūpāt paridhānīyāyai ca |
7.14.d: स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपाभ्याम् यच् च अनन्तरम् अनुरूपात् परिधानीयायै च ।
7.14.m: [The calls are made] at the strophe and antistrophe, and at that which immediately follows the antistrophe, and at the concluding verse.

7.14.s: anurūpād anantaraḥ pragāthas tasmād ūrdhvam pañcamam madhyaṃdine |
7.14.d: अनुरूपाद् अनन्तरः प्रगाथस् तस्माद् ऊर्ध्वम् पञ्चमम् मध्यंदिने ।
7.14.m: The pragātha immediately follows the antistrophe; after that, a fifth [call] at the midday [pressing].
At night, [it is made] after the opening of the hymn for all.

7.14.s: yadā adhvaryur āha praśāstaḥ prasuhi ity om sarpata iti praśāsta āha |
7.14.d: यदा अध्वर्युर् आह प्रशास्तः प्रसुहि इत्य् ओम् सर्पत इति प्रशास्त आह ।
7.14.m: When the Adhvaryu says, "O director, prompt [us]!", the Praśāstṛ says, "Om, glide forward!"

7.14.s: dakṣiṇa āvṛto aparayā dvārā nihsarpanty uttareṇa udumbarīm dakṣiṇena brahmā |
7.14.d: दक्षिण आवृतो अपरया द्वारा निह्सर्पन्त्य् उत्तरेण उदुम्बरीम् दक्षिणेन ब्रह्मा ।
7.14.m: Turning to the right, they glide out through the western door, to the north of the Udumbara post; the Brahman priest [glides] to the south.

7.14.s: mādhyaṃdināya savanāya yathā nihsṛptam prasṛpya yathā āsanam upaviśanti |
7.14.d: माध्यंदिनाय सवनाय यथा निह्सृप्तम् प्रसृप्य यथा आसनम् उपविशन्ति ।
7.14.m: Having glided forth for the midday pressing in the manner they glided out, they sit down according to their seats.

7.15.m: At the beginning of the midday pressing, they press the king [Soma].

7.15.s: grāvastut pūrvayā dvārā havir dhāne prapadya uttarasya havir dhānasya dakṣiṇam cakram agreṇa dakṣiṇā tiṣṭhan soma upanahanena mukham pariveṣṭya grāva ghoṣam śrutvā asampreṣito abhiṣṭauty asaṃtanvann ardharcaśo anavānam vā |
7.15.d: ग्रावस्तुत् पूर्वया द्वारा हविर् धाने प्रपद्य उत्तरस्य हविर् धानस्य दक्षिणम् चक्रम् अग्रेण दक्षिणा तिष्ठन् सोम उपनहनेन मुखम् परिवेष्ट्य ग्राव घोषम् श्रुत्वा असम्प्रेषितो अभिष्टौत्य् असंतन्वन्न् अर्धर्चशो अनवानम् वा ।
7.15.m: The Grāvastut priest, having entered the two cart-sheds through the eastern door, standing south in front of the southern wheel of the northern cart-shed, having wrapped his mouth with the Soma-wrapping cloth, having heard the sound of the pressing stones, recites without being prompted, not joining [the verses], half-verse by half-verse, or without taking a breath.

7.15.s: abhi tvā deva savitar yuñjate mana uta yuñjate dhiya ā tū na indra kṣumantam ā no bhara dakṣiṇena upa kramasva ā bhara |
7.15.d: अभि त्वा देव सवितर् युञ्जते मन उत युञ्जते धिय आ तू न इन्द्र क्षुमन्तम् आ नो भर दक्षिणेन उप क्रमस्व आ भर ।
7.15.m: "Towards thee, divine Savitṛ...", "They yoke the mind and they yoke the thoughts...", "Now to us, O Indra, rich in cattle...", "Bring to us with the right [hand]...", "Step near, bring..."

7.15.s: ā pyāyasva sametu ta ity āpyāyitavatīnām tisṛṇām prathamām abhiṣṭutya arbudasya dve |
7.15.d: आ प्यायस्व समेतु त इत्य् आप्यायितवतीनाम् तिसृणाम् प्रथमाम् अभिष्टुत्य अर्बुदस्य द्वे ।
7.15.m: Having recited the first of the three [verses] containing the word 'swell', [namely] "Swell up, may [vitality] gather to thee", [he recites] two [verses] of the Arbuda hymn.
Having recited the second, [he recites] two [verses] of the Arbuda hymn.
Having recited the third, [he recites] one [verse] of the Arbuda hymn.

7.15.s: mṛjanti tvā daśa kṣipa etam u tyam daśa kṣipa etam mṛjanti marjyam iti mṛṣṭavatīr abhiṣṭutya |
7.15.d: मृजन्ति त्वा दश क्षिप एतम् उ त्यम् दश क्षिप एतम् मृजन्ति मर्ज्यम् इति मृष्टवतीर् अभिष्टुत्य ।
7.15.m: Having recited the [verses] containing the word 'cleanse': "Ten fingers cleanse thee...", "This very one the ten fingers...", "They cleanse him, the one to be cleansed...";

7.15.s: ā kalaśā anūṣatā kalaśeṣu dhāvati pari pra soma te rasa iti kalaśavatīr abhiṣṭutya |
7.15.d: आ कलशा अनूषता कलशेषु धावति परि प्र सोम ते रस इति कलशवतीर् अभिष्टुत्य ।
7.15.m: having recited the [verses] containing the word 'jar': "Into the jars they have sung...", "He runs into the jars...", "Round about, O Soma, thy juice...",

7.15.s: āpyāyitavatī prabhṛty evam vihṛto dvitīyo api savaḥ | ṣaṣṭhī prabhṛtayaḥ pañca arbudasya |
7.15.d: आप्यायितवती प्रभृत्य् एवम् विहृतो द्वितीयो अपि सवः । षष्ठी प्रभृतयः पञ्च अर्बुदस्य ।
7.15.m: beginning from the verse containing 'swell', the second pressing [round] is likewise distributed; five [verses] of the Arbuda hymn, beginning with the sixth [are recited].

7.15.s: evam vihṛtas tṛtīyo api savaḥ | tisro arbudasya ekādaśī prabhṛtayaḥ |
7.15.d: एवम् विहृतस् तृतीयो अपि सवः । तिस्रो अर्बुदस्य एकादशी प्रभृतयः ।
7.15.m: The third pressing [round] is likewise distributed; three [verses] of the Arbuda hymn, beginning with the eleventh [are recited].

7.15.s: yasmin save bṛhat śabdam kuryur bṛhad vadantī iti tatra |
7.15.d: यस्मिन् सवे बृहत् शब्दम् कुर्युर् बृहद् वदन्ती इति तत्र ।
7.15.m: At whichever pressing [round] they make a loud noise, there [he recites] "Uttering loudly...".

7.15.s: vitate pavitre pavitram ta iti dve vi yat pavitram ity ekā |
7.15.d: वितते पवित्रे पवित्रम् त इति द्वे वि यत् पवित्रम् इत्य् एका ।
7.15.m: When the filter is spread out: two [verses], "Thy filter...", and one, "When the filter...".

7.15.s: prāsya dhārāḥ pra dhārā asya pra te dhārā iti prakṣarantīṣu dhārāsu |
7.15.d: प्रास्य धाराः प्र धारा अस्य प्र ते धारा इति प्रक्षरन्तीषु धारासु ।
7.15.m: While the streams are flowing forth: "Forth his streams...", "Forth the streams of this...", "Forth thy streams...".
While the cups are being drawn, whichever Pavamāna verses he may desire.

7.15.s: indrāya indo marutvata iti tisro niyacchati |
7.15.d: इन्द्राय इन्दो मरुत्वत इति तिस्रो नियच्छति ।
7.15.m: He holds back three [verses]: "For Indra, O drop, accompanied by the Maruts...".

7.15.s: uttame grahe gṛhīte arbudasya uttamayā paridhāya ādāya uṣṇīṣam utsṛjyate |
7.15.d: उत्तमे ग्रहे गृहीते अर्बुदस्य उत्तमया परिधाय आदाय उष्णीषम् उत्सृज्यते ।
7.15.m: When the last cup has been drawn, having concluded with the last [verse] of the Arbuda hymn, taking off the turban, he is dismissed.
On the last day of sattras and ahīnas, however,
he may recite the Arbuda hymn pure [without intercalations].

7.16.s: mādhyaṃdine stute pavamānena dadhi gharmeṇa caranti yadi pravargyavān |
7.16.d: माध्यंदिने स्तुते पवमानेन दधि घर्मेण चरन्ति यदि प्रवर्ग्यवान् ।
7.16.m: When the midday [stotra] has been praised with the Pavamāna chant, they proceed with the curd-and-ghee offering, if [the sacrifice is] provided with the Pravargya rite.

7.16.s: hotar vadasva ity ukta uttiṣṭhata ava paśyata iti prathamām abhiṣṭauti |
7.16.d: होतर् वदस्व इत्य् उक्त उत्तिष्ठत अव पश्यत इति प्रथमाम् अभिष्टौति ।
7.16.m: When told, "Hotṛ, speak!", he recites the first [verse]: "Stand up, look down...".

7.16.s: śrātam havir ity ukte dvitīyām sūktasya |
7.16.d: श्रातम् हविर् इत्य् उक्ते द्वितीयाम् सूक्तस्य ।
7.16.m: When it is said, "The oblation is cooked", [he recites] the second [verse] of the hymn.

7.16.s: dadhi gharmasya yaja ity uktas tṛtīyayā yajati |
7.16.d: दधि घर्मस्य यज इत्य् उक्तस् तृतीयया यजति ।
7.16.m: When told, "Recite the offering verse of the curd-and-ghee offering!", he recites the offering verse with the third [verse].
He recites each one without breathing, with the praṇava.

7.16.s: dadhi gharmasya agne vīhi ity anuvaṣaṭ kāraḥ |
7.16.d: दधि घर्मस्य अग्ने वीहि इत्य् अनुवषट् कारः ।
7.16.m: The secondary vaṣaṭ-call is: "O Agni, enjoy the curd-and-ghee offering!".

7.16.s: mayi tyad indriyam bṛhan mayi dakṣo mayi kratuḥ | gharmas triśug virocata ākūtyā manasā saha | virājā jyotiṣā saha tasya doham aśīmahi | iti bhakṣa mantraḥ |
7.16.d: मयि त्यद् इन्द्रियम् बृहन् मयि दक्षो मयि क्रतुः । घर्मस् त्रिशुग् विरोचत आकूत्या मनसा सह । विराजा ज्योतिषा सह तस्य दोहम् अशीमहि । इति भक्ष मन्त्रः ।
7.16.m: "In me be that great faculty of Indra, in me ability, in me ritual insight; may the three-gleaming Gharma shine forth along with intention, with mind, with the Virāj, with light; may we attain its milk"—this is the mantra for consuming.

7.16.s: paśu puroḷāśena caritvā ataḥ puroḷāśaiḥ savanīyaiś caranti |
7.16.d: पशु पुरोऌआशेन चरित्वा अतः पुरोऌआशैः सवनीयैश् चरन्ति ।
7.16.m: Having proceeded with the animal sacrificial cake, they proceed from here with the offering cakes of the pressing.

7.17.m: "Of the midday pressing..." is the introductory verse.
"At the midday pressing..." is [the verse] for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.
"The god has been pressed" (RV 8.43.20ff.) is the hymn recited while [the Soma] is being drawn up.

7.17.s: hotā yakṣad indram mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya iti praiṣaḥ |
7.17.d: होता यक्षद् इन्द्रम् माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य इति प्रैषः ।
7.17.m: "May the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra of the midday pressing" is the ritual summons.

7.17.s: pibā somam abhi yam ugra iti yajati |
7.17.d: पिबा सोमम् अभि यम् उग्र इति यजति ।
7.17.m: He recites the offering verse: "Drink the Soma, towards which, O fierce one..." (RV 6.40.1).
The second [verse] belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa.
The third belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.
"Thine is this Soma" (RV 1.15.3) belongs to the Neṣṭṛ.

7.17.s: indrāya somāḥ pradivo vidānā ity acchāvākasya |
7.17.d: इन्द्राय सोमाः प्रदिवो विदाना इत्य् अच्छावाकस्य ।
7.17.m: "For Indra the Somas known from of old" (RV 9.88.1) belongs to the Acchāvāka.
"Filled is his..." (RV 4.9.7) belongs to the Āgnīdhra.

7.17.s: na dvidevatya ṛtu yājā uttarayoḥ savanayoḥ |
7.17.d: न द्विदेवत्य ऋतु याजा उत्तरयोः सवनयोः ।
7.17.m: There are no dual-deity season-offerings in the two later pressings.
There is no ritual action outside [the sanctuary] for the Acchāvāka.
The rest is the same as the morning pressing.
Having invited the iḷā and consumed the set-out cups;
He should give one hundred and twelve cows;
or starting from twenty-one, according to what is available.

7.18.s: agnaye tvā mahyam varuṇo dadātu so amṛtatvam aśīya | āyur dātra edhi mayo mahyam patigṛhṇata iti hiraṇyam pratigṛhṇāti |
7.18.d: अग्नये त्वा मह्यम् वरुणो ददातु सो अमृतत्वम् अशीय । आयुर् दात्र एधि मयो मह्यम् पतिगृह्णत इति हिरण्यम् प्रतिगृह्णाति ।
7.18.m: He receives gold with: "May Varuṇa give thee to me for Agni; may I attain immortality. Be thou life to the giver, delight to me who receives!"

7.18.s: rudrāya tvā mahyam varuṇo dadātu so amṛtatvam aśīya | gaur dātra edhi mayo mahyam patigṛhṇat iti gāḥ |
7.18.d: रुद्राय त्वा मह्यम् वरुणो ददातु सो अमृतत्वम् अशीय । गौर् दात्र एधि मयो मह्यम् पतिगृह्णत् इति गाः ।
7.18.m: Cows with: "May Varuṇa give thee to me for Rudra; may I attain immortality. Be thou a cow to the giver, delight to me who receives!"

7.18.s: bṛhaspataye tvā mahyam varuṇo dadātu so amṛtatvam aśīya | tvag dātra edhi mayo mahyam pratigṛhṇata iti vāsaḥ |
7.18.d: बृहस्पतये त्वा मह्यम् वरुणो ददातु सो अमृतत्वम् अशीय । त्वग् दात्र एधि मयो मह्यम् प्रतिगृह्णत इति वासः ।
7.18.m: A garment with: "May Varuṇa give thee to me for Bṛhaspati; may I attain immortality. Be thou a hide to the giver, delight to me who receives!"

7.18.s: yamāya tvā mahyam varuṇo dadātu so amṛtatvam aśīya | hayo dātra edhi mayo mahyam pratigṛhṇata ity eka śapham |
7.18.d: यमाय त्वा मह्यम् वरुणो ददातु सो अमृतत्वम् अशीय । हयो दात्र एधि मयो मह्यम् प्रतिगृह्णत इत्य् एक शफम् ।
7.18.m: A single-hoofed animal with: "May Varuṇa give thee to me for Yama; may I attain immortality. Be thou a horse to the giver, delight to me who receives!"

7.18.s: prajāpataye tvā mahyam varuṇo dadātu so amṛtatvam aśīya | prāṇo dātra edhi mayo mahyam pratigṛhṇata ity anyat |
7.18.d: प्रजापतये त्वा मह्यम् वरुणो ददातु सो अमृतत्वम् अशीय । प्राणो दात्र एधि मयो मह्यम् प्रतिगृह्णत इत्य् अन्यत् ।
7.18.m: Anything else with: "May Varuṇa give thee to me for Prajāpati; may I attain immortality. Be thou breath to the giver, delight to me who receives!"

7.18.s: ko adāt kasmā adād ity anumantrayate prāṇi |
7.18.d: को अदात् कस्मा अदाद् इत्य् अनुमन्त्रयते प्राणि ।
7.18.m: Over a living being he mutters: "Who gave? To whom did he give?..."

7.18.s: asmad rātā madhumatīr devatrā gacchata pradātāram ā viśata iti dattvā japati |
7.18.d: अस्मद् राता मधुमतीर् देवत्रा गच्छत प्रदातारम् आ विशत इति दत्त्वा जपति ।
7.18.m: Having given [it], he mutters: "Given by us, full of sweetness, go to the gods; enter into the giver!"

7.19.m: When addressed: "[Recite] for Indra accompanied by the Maruts!",
"O Indra accompanied by the Maruts..." (RV 3.51.7) is the introductory verse.

7.19.s: hotā yakṣad indram marutvantam iti praiṣaḥ |
7.19.d: होता यक्षद् इन्द्रम् मरुत्वन्तम् इति प्रैषः ।
7.19.m: "May the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra accompanied by the Maruts" is the ritual summons.
He recites the offering verse: "In concord, O Indra, with the host..." (RV 3.47.2).
Having consumed it, he recites the Marutvatīya-śastra.

7.19.s: adhvaryo śoṃśāvo ity āhāvaḥ śastra ādau mādhyaṃdine savane |
7.19.d: अध्वर्यो शोंशावो इत्य् आहावः शस्त्र आदौ माध्यंदिने सवने ।
7.19.m: "Adhvaryu, let us two recite" is the call at the beginning of the śastra in the midday pressing.
The one belonging to the morning pressing is [used] within the śastra.

7.19.s: ā tvā ratham yathā ūtaya iti prātipadam tṛcam śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: आ त्वा रथम् यथा ऊतय इति प्रातिपदम् तृचम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: Having recited the opening triplet: "Hither to thee, like a chariot for aid..." (RV 8.68.1–3) and called;

7.19.s: idma vaso sutam andha ity anucaram tṛcam śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: इद्म वसो सुतम् अन्ध इत्य् अनुचरम् तृचम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: having recited the following triplet: "This pressed food, O bountiful one..." (RV 8.68.4–6) and called;

7.19.s: indra nedīya ed ihi iti indra nihavam pragātham śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: इन्द्र नेदीय एद् इहि इति इन्द्र निहवम् प्रगाथम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: having recited the pragātha of the invocation of Indra: "Come right close, O Indra..." (RV 8.53.5–6) and called;

7.19.s: pra nūnam brahmaṇaspatir iti brāhmaṇaspatyam pragātham śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: प्र नूनम् ब्रह्मणस्पतिर् इति ब्राह्मणस्पत्यम् प्रगाथम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: having recited the pragātha to Brahmaṇaspati: "Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati..." (RV 1.40.5–6) and called;

7.19.s: agnir netā ity ekām śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: अग्निर् नेता इत्य् एकाम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: having recited the single verse: "Agni is the leader..." (RV 3.20.4) and called;

7.19.s: tvam soma kratubhir ity ekām śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: त्वम् सोम क्रतुभिर् इत्य् एकाम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: having recited the single verse: "Thou, O Soma, by thy wisdom..." (RV 1.91.2) and called;

7.19.s: pinvanty apa ity ekām śastvā āhūya |
7.19.d: पिन्वन्त्य् अप इत्य् एकाम् शस्त्वा आहूय ।
7.19.m: having recited the single verse: "The waters swell..." (RV 1.64.6) and called;

7.19.s: janiṣṭhā ugra iti ṣaṭ śastvā āhūya nividam |
7.19.d: जनिष्ठा उग्र इति षट् शस्त्वा आहूय निविदम् ।
7.19.m: having recited six [verses of]: "Thou wast born, O fierce one..." (RV 3.49.1–6) and called, [he inserts] the nivid.
The first response in this [śastra] contains the word 'mad' (intoxicating).
In hymns with an uneven number of verses, [the nivid is inserted] after reciting more by one [verse];
Leaving the last verses [unrecited] in the third pressing,
he recites the nivids verse-foot by verse-foot, detached.

7.19.s: sūkta śeṣam śastvā āhūya uttamayā paridhāya uktha vīryam japitvā ye tvāhihatya iti yajati |
7.19.d: सूक्त शेषम् शस्त्वा आहूय उत्तमया परिधाय उक्थ वीर्यम् जपित्वा ये त्वाहिहत्य इति यजति ।
7.19.m: Having recited the remainder of the hymn, called, concluded with the final verse, and muttered the virility of the uktha, he recites the offering verse: "Who, in the slaying of Ahi, thee..." (RV 3.47.5).

7.20.m: The Rathantara chant is the pṛṣṭha-sāman of the Niṣkevalya-śastra;

7.20.s: abhi tvā śūra abhi tvā pūrva pītaya iti stotriya anurūpau pragāthau rathantarasya |
7.20.d: अभि त्वा शूर अभि त्वा पूर्व पीतय इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ प्रगाथौ रथन्तरस्य ।
7.20.m: "Unto thee, O hero..." (RV 7.32.22–23) and "unto thee, for the first drinking..." (RV 8.88.1–2) are the stotriya and anurūpa pragāthas of the Rathantara chant;

7.20.s: tvām iddhi havāmahe tvam hy ehi cerava iti bṛhataḥ |
7.20.d: त्वाम् इद्धि हवामहे त्वम् ह्य् एहि चेरव इति बृहतः ।
7.20.m: "Thee indeed we call upon..." (RV 6.46.1–2) and "thou indeed come, O swift one..." (RV 8.88.3–4) of the Bṛhat chant.

7.20.s: pibā sutasya rasina iti pragātho rathantarasya |
7.20.d: पिबा सुतस्य रसिन इति प्रगाथो रथन्तरस्य ।
7.20.m: "Drink of the pressed, sapful..." (RV 8.3.1–2) is the pragātha of the Rathantara chant;
"May he hear both..." (RV 6.19.1–2) of the Bṛhat chant.

7.20.s: indrasya nu vīryāṇi iti rathantara pṛṣṭhe |
7.20.d: इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि इति रथन्तर पृष्ठे ।
7.20.m: "Of Indra now the heroic deeds..." (RV 1.32) when the Rathantara is the pṛṣṭha;

7.20.s: tam u ṣṭuhi iti bṛhat pṛṣṭhe |
7.20.d: तम् उ ष्टुहि इति बृहत् पृष्ठे ।
7.20.m: "Praise him..." (RV 6.18) when the Bṛhat is the pṛṣṭha.
He should recite the concluding verse in a lower tone.

7.20.s: uktha vīryam japitvā pibā somam indr amandatu tvā iti yajati |
7.20.d: उक्थ वीर्यम् जपित्वा पिबा सोमम् इन्द्र् अमन्दतु त्वा इति यजति ।
7.20.m: Having muttered the essence of the uktha, he recites the offering verse: "Drink the Soma, let it gladden you, O Indra..."

7.21.s: rathantara pṛṣṭhe yaḥ sūktāt pūrvaḥ pragātas tam uddhṛtya bṛhato yonim śaṃsati |
7.21.d: रथन्तर पृष्ठे यः सूक्तात् पूर्वः प्रगातस् तम् उद्धृत्य बृहतो योनिम् शंसति ।
7.21.m: When the Rathantara chant is the pṛṣṭha-sāman, taking out the pragātha that precedes the hymn, he recites the womb (yoni) of the Bṛhat chant.
When the Bṛhat chant is the pṛṣṭha-sāman, [he recites the womb] of the Rathantara chant.
In the subsequent sacrificial forms, [he recites it] after the chant-pragātha (sāmapragātha).
They call this 'the recitation of the womb' (yonyanuśaṃsana).

7.21.s: bṛhad rathantarayor eva anuśaṃsed iti ha sma kauṣītakiḥ |
7.21.d: बृहद् रथन्तरयोर् एव अनुशंसेद् इति ह स्म कौषीतकिः ।
7.21.m: Kauṣītaki used to say: 'One should recite it only in the case of the Bṛhat and Rathantara chants.'

7.21.s: parimita śasyaḥ prākṛto agniṣṭomas tasmāt pragātham uddharati |
7.21.d: परिमित शस्यः प्राकृतो अग्निष्टोमस् तस्मात् प्रगाथम् उद्धरति ।
7.21.m: The archetypal Agniṣṭoma has a measured recitation; therefore, he takes out the pragātha.

7.21.s: stotriyāya āhāvo anurūpāya dhāyyāyai pragāthāya sūktāya nivide paridhānīyāyai ca |
7.21.d: स्तोत्रियाय आहावो अनुरूपाय धाय्यायै प्रगाथाय सूक्ताय निविदे परिधानीयायै च ।
7.21.m: There is a call (āhāva) for the stotriya, for the anurūpa, for the dhāyyā, for the pragātha, for the hymn, for the nivid, and for the concluding verse.

7.22.m: The Vāmadevya chant belongs to the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.

7.22.s: kayā naś citraḥ kayā tvam na ūtyā iti stotriya anurūpau |
7.22.d: कया नश् चित्रः कया त्वम् न ऊत्या इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ ।
7.22.m: "kayā naś citraḥ" and "kayā tvam na ūtyā" are the stotriya and anurūpa [pragāthas].

7.22.s: kas tam indra iti sāma pragāthaḥ |
7.22.d: कस् तम् इन्द्र इति साम प्रगाथः ।

7.22.m: [The inserted verse is] "evā tvam indra vajrinn atra".

7.22.s: uśan nu ṣu ṇa iti yajati |
7.22.d: उशन् नु षु ण इति यजति ।

7.23.m: The Naudhasa chant belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin when the Rathantara chant is the pṛṣṭha-sāman.

7.23.s: tam vo dasmam tat tvā yāmi suvīryam iti stotriya anurūpau pragāthau naudhasasya |
7.23.d: तम् वो दस्मम् तत् त्वा यामि सुवीर्यम् इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ प्रगाथौ नौधसस्य ।
7.23.m: "tam vo dasmam" and "tat tvā yāmi suvīryam" are the stotriya and anurūpa pragāthas of the Naudhasa chant.

7.23.s: abhi pra vaḥ pra su śrutam iti śyaitasya |
7.23.d: अभि प्र वः प्र सु श्रुतम् इति श्यैतस्य ।
7.23.m: "abhi pra vaḥ" and "pra su śrutam" are [the stotriya and anurūpa pragāthas] of the Śyaita chant.

7.23.s: ud u tye madhumattamā iti sāma pragāthaḥ |
7.23.d: उद् उ त्ये मधुमत्तमा इति साम प्रगाथः ।
7.23.m: "ud u tye madhumattamāḥ" is the chant-pragātha.
[The hymn is] "indraḥ pūrbhit" for the Naudhasa chant.

7.23.s: asāvi somaḥ puru hūta iti śyaite |
7.23.d: असावि सोमः पुरु हूत इति श्यैते ।
7.23.m: [The hymn is] "asāvi somaḥ puruhūta" for the Śyaita chant.

7.24.s: tarobhir vas taraṇir it siṣāsati iti stotriya anurūpau pragāthau |
7.24.d: तरोभिर् वस् तरणिर् इत् सिषासति इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ प्रगाथौ ।
7.24.m: "tarobhir vaḥ" and "taraṇir it siṣāsati" are the stotriya and anurūpa pragāthas.

7.24.s: ud inv asya ricyata iti sāma pragāthaḥ |
7.24.d: उद् इन्व् अस्य रिच्यत इति साम प्रगाथः ।
7.24.m: "ud inv asya ricyate" is the chant-pragātha.
He recites the offering verse: "pibā vardhasva".

7.25.m: for the most part [the pragāthas are recited] not as they are handed down [in the Saṃhitā].

7.25.s: bṛhatī pūrvā kakub vā sato bṛhaty uttarā tam pragātaḥ ity ācakṣate |
7.25.d: बृहती पूर्वा ककुब् वा सतो बृहत्य् उत्तरा तम् प्रगातः इत्य् आचक्षते ।
7.25.m: When a Bṛhatī precedes or a Kakubh precedes, and a Sato-bṛhatī follows, they call it a pragātha.
A Bārhata pragātha has a Bṛhatī preceding;

7.25.s: bṛhatīm śastvā uttamam pādam pratyādāya uttarasyāḥ prathamena avasāya dvitīyena praṇutya tam pratyādāya tṛtīyena avasāya uttamena praṇauti |
7.25.d: बृहतीम् शस्त्वा उत्तमम् पादम् प्रत्यादाय उत्तरस्याः प्रथमेन अवसाय द्वितीयेन प्रणुत्य तम् प्रत्यादाय तृतीयेन अवसाय उत्तमेन प्रणौति ।
7.25.m: Having recited the Bṛhatī, taking up again the last pāda, pausing after the first [pāda] of the following [verse], pronouncing the praṇava with the second, taking that up again, pausing after the third, he pronounces the praṇava with the last [pāda].

7.25.s: tās tisro bhavanti bṛhatī pūrva uttare kakubhau |
7.25.d: तास् तिस्रो भवन्ति बृहती पूर्व उत्तरे ककुभौ ।
7.25.m: These become three: the first a Bṛhatī, the following two Kakubhs.

7.25.s: hotrakāṇām ca yatra ete pṛṣṭhe pragāthasthe |
7.25.d: होत्रकाणाम् च यत्र एते पृष्ठे प्रगाथस्थे ।
7.25.m: and in the recitations of the minor Hotṛs (hotrakas) where these two [chants] are placed in the pṛṣṭha-pragāthas;
and in the Indranihava and Brāhmaṇaspatya hymns.
Elsewhere than this, in the case of Bārhata pragāthas:

7.25.s: bṛhatīm śastvā uttamam pādam dviḥ pratyādāya avasāya ardharcena uttarasyāḥ praṇutya dvitīyam pādam dviḥ pratyādāya avasāya uttamena ardharcena praṇauti |
7.25.d: बृहतीम् शस्त्वा उत्तमम् पादम् द्विः प्रत्यादाय अवसाय अर्धर्चेन उत्तरस्याः प्रणुत्य द्वितीयम् पादम् द्विः प्रत्यादाय अवसाय उत्तमेन अर्धर्चेन प्रणौति ।
7.25.m: Having recited the Bṛhatī, taking up again the last pāda twice and pausing, pronouncing the praṇava with a half-verse of the following [verse], taking up again the second pāda twice and pausing, he pronounces the praṇava with the last half-verse. / These become three Bṛhatīs.

7.25.s: tās tisro bṛhatyaḥ | uttamam kakubhaḥ pratyādatte |
7.25.d: तास् तिस्रो बृहत्यः । उत्तमम् ककुभः प्रत्यादत्ते ।
7.25.m: He takes up again the last [pāda] of the Kakubh,

7.25.s: stotriyatvād anurūpatvād vā | etam dharmam pragāthā labhante |
7.25.d: स्तोत्रियत्वाद् अनुरूपत्वाद् वा । एतम् धर्मम् प्रगाथा लभन्ते ।
7.25.m: Pragāthas receive this modification (dharma) by virtue of being a stotriya or an anurūpa.

7.26.m: The Indranihava is not a stotriya,

7.26.s: dvābhyām avasāya dvābhyām avasāya ekena praṇauti paṅktīnām |
7.26.d: द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय एकेन प्रणौति पङ्क्तीनाम् ।
7.26.m: In the case of Paṅkti verses, pausing after two [pādas], and pausing after two [pādas], he pronounces the praṇava with one [pāda].

7.26.s: apcchas triṣṭub jagatīnām akṣara paṅktīnām dvipadānām ca |
7.26.d: अप्च्छस् त्रिष्टुब् जगतीनाम् अक्षर पङ्क्तीनाम् द्विपदानाम् च ।
7.26.m: [The same applies] to Triṣṭubh and Jagatī verses lacking a quarter (apcchaḥ), to Akṣarapaṅktis, and to Dvipadā verses.
The second and the fourth [pādas] are accompanied by the praṇava.

7.26.s: yās tu pañca padās traiṣṭubhe prāye jāgate vā yatra punaḥ padam syāt tau tatra samasyen na padena punaḥ padasya viprayogo asti |
7.26.d: यास् तु पञ्च पदास् त्रैष्टुभे प्राये जागते वा यत्र पुनः पदम् स्यात् तौ तत्र समस्येन् न पदेन पुनः पदस्य विप्रयोगो अस्ति ।
7.26.m: However, as for five-pāda verses within a Triṣṭubh or Jagatī course, where there is a repeated pāda (punaḥpada), there he should combine those two: there is no separation of a repeated pāda from a pāda.

7.26.s: dvābhyām avasāya dvābhyām avasāya dvābhyām praṇauti ṣaṭ padānām punaḥ padānām |
7.26.d: द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय द्वाभ्याम् प्रणौति षट् पदानाम् पुनः पदानाम् ।
7.26.m: In the case of six-pāda verses with a repeated pāda, pausing after two [pādas], pausing after two [pādas], he pronounces the praṇava with two.

7.26.s: dvābhyām avasāya apunaḥ padānām ekena praṇauti dvābhyām avasāya ekena |
7.26.d: द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय अपुनः पदानाम् एकेन प्रणौति द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय एकेन ।
7.26.m: In the case of verses without a repeated pāda, pausing after two, he pronounces the praṇava with one; pausing after two, [he pronounces the praṇava] with one.
The [pāda] with which the praṇava is pronounced, however, consists of eight syllables.

7.26.s: ekena avasāya sapta padānām dvābhyām praṇauti dvābhyām avasāya dvābhyām |
7.26.d: एकेन अवसाय सप्त पदानाम् द्वाभ्याम् प्रणौति द्वाभ्याम् अवसाय द्वाभ्याम् ।
7.26.m: In the case of seven-pāda verses, pausing after one, he pronounces the praṇava with two; pausing after two, [he pronounces the praṇava] with two.

7.26.s: prathameṣu rātri paryāyeṣu gāyatrāṇām stotriya anurūpāṇām prathamān pādān abhyasyanti |
7.26.d: प्रथमेषु रात्रि पर्यायेषु गायत्राणाम् स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपाणाम् प्रथमान् पादान् अभ्यस्यन्ति ।
7.26.m: In the first rounds of the night (rātriparyāya), they repeat the first pādas of the Gāyatrī stotriya and anurūpa verses.
The middle [quarters] in the middle ones;
Or half-verse by half-verse during the morning pressing,
Except for the stotriya, anurūpa, and pragātha verses.

7.27.m: The subsequent virāj has four quarters;
The aticchandas meters have six or seven.

7.27.s: sa hi śardho na mārutam ity aṣṭau |
7.27.d: स हि शर्धो न मारुतम् इत्य् अष्टौ ।
7.27.m: [The hymn beginning] 'sa hi śardho na mārutam' has eight.
These [quarters] generally consist of eight syllables.
Those of the jagatī consist of twelve syllables;
And the third [quarter] of the uṣṇih and the bṛhatī;
And the first and third [quarters] of the satobṛhatī;

7.27.s: uttarasyā daśa akṣarāḥ | tām akṣara paṅktir ity apy ācakṣate | pañcabhiḥ pañca akṣaraiḥ pada paṅktiḥ | ṣaḷ apy aṣṭa akṣarā jagatyāḥ | ekena dvābhyām ity ūnake nicṛt |
7.27.d: उत्तरस्या दश अक्षराः । ताम् अक्षर पङ्क्तिर् इत्य् अप्य् आचक्षते । पञ्चभिः पञ्च अक्षरैः पद पङ्क्तिः । षऌ अप्य् अष्ट अक्षरा जगत्याः । एकेन द्वाभ्याम् इत्य् ऊनके निचृत् ।
7.27.m:
Those of the triṣṭubh and the [earlier] virāj consist of eleven syllables. / Those of the subsequent [virāj] consist of ten syllables; / that they also call akṣarapaṅkti. / The padapaṅkti consists of five five-syllable [quarters]. / Six [quarters] of eight syllables also make a jagatī.
When deficient by one or two [syllables], it is a nicṛt;

7.27.s: sampādya pāda bhāgena āhāryasya ṛcaḥ sammitās tasya pāda bhāgena sampannāḥ |
7.27.d: सम्पाद्य पाद भागेन आहार्यस्य ऋचः सम्मितास् तस्य पाद भागेन सम्पन्नाः ।
7.27.m: By producing [the meter] through the fraction of a quarter, verses of an imported [meter] are measured [and] accomplished through that fraction of a quarter.

7.27.s: gāyatry uṣṇihāv anuṣṭub bṛhatyau paṅktiś ca triṣṭub jagatyāv ity ānupūrvyam chandasām catur viṃśaty akṣara ādīnām catur uttarāṇām catur uttarāṇām |
7.27.d: गायत्र्य् उष्णिहाव् अनुष्टुब् बृहत्यौ पङ्क्तिश् च त्रिष्टुब् जगत्याव् इत्य् आनुपूर्व्यम् छन्दसाम् चतुर् विंशत्य् अक्षर आदीनाम् चतुर् उत्तराणाम् चतुर् उत्तराणाम् ।
7.27.m: Gāyatrī, uṣṇih, anuṣṭubh, bṛhatī, and paṅkti, triṣṭubh, and jagatī—this is the order of the meters, beginning with twenty-four syllables, each increasing by four [syllables].

8.1.s: yathā madhyaṃdināya evam ūrdhvam madhyaṃdināt prasarpanti |
8.1.d: यथा मध्यंदिनाय एवम् ऊर्ध्वम् मध्यंदिनात् प्रसर्पन्ति ।
8.1.m: As [they proceed] to the midday [pressing], thus after the midday [pressing] they creep forth.

8.1.s: ādau tṛtīya savanasya āditya graheṇa caranti |
8.1.d: आदौ तृतीय सवनस्य आदित्य ग्रहेण चरन्ति ।
8.1.m: At the beginning of the third pressing, they perform [the offering] with the Aditya-graha.
'hotā yakṣad ādityān' is the ritual summons;
He recites the offering verse: 'ādityāso aditiḥ'.
He neither looks after the oblation nor consumes [his portion];

8.1.s: ārbhavena stute pavamānena manotād iḷā antam pauś karma kṛtvā ataḥ puroḷāśaiḥ savanīyaiś caranti |
8.1.d: आर्भवेन स्तुते पवमानेन मनोताद् इऌआ अन्तम् पौश् कर्म कृत्वा अतः पुरोऌआशैः सवनीयैश् चरन्ति ।
8.1.m: When the Ārbhava-pavamāna has been chanted, having performed the animal rite from the Manotā hymn up to the iḷā, they then perform [the offerings] with the cakes belonging to the pressing.

8.2.m: 'tṛtīye dhānāḥ savane' is the introductory verse;
'agne tṛtīye savane' is [the verse] for the Sviṣṭakṛt.

8.2.s: iha upa yata ity unnīyamāna sūktam |
8.2.d: इह उप यत इत्य् उन्नीयमान सूक्तम् ।
8.2.m: 'ihopeyāta' is the hymn recited while [the soma cups] are drawn up.

8.2.s: hotā yakṣad indram tṛtīyasya savanasya iti praiṣaḥ |
8.2.d: होता यक्षद् इन्द्रम् तृतीयस्य सवनस्य इति प्रैषः ।
8.2.m: 'hotā yakṣad indram tṛtīyasya savanasya' is the ritual summons;
He recites the offering verse: 'indra ṛbhubhir vājavadbhiḥ'.

8.2.s: indrā varuṇā sutapāv iti maitrā varuṇaḥ |
8.2.d: इन्द्रा वरुणा सुतपाव् इति मैत्रा वरुणः ।

8.2.m: The rest is the same as the morning pressing.

8.2.s: iḷām upahūya prasthitān bhakṣayitvā puroḷāśasya parivāpa miśrasya nārāśaṃsānām sannānām yathā camasam dakṣiṇatas trīṃs trīn piṇḍān upāsyanty atra pitaro mādayadhvam yathā bhāgam pitara āvṛṣāyadhvam iti pṇḍe piṇḍe |
8.2.d: इऌआम् उपहूय प्रस्थितान् भक्षयित्वा पुरोऌआशस्य परिवाप मिश्रस्य नाराशंसानाम् सन्नानाम् यथा चमसम् दक्षिणतस् त्रींस् त्रीन् पिण्डान् उपास्यन्त्य् अत्र पितरो मादयध्वम् यथा भागम् पितर आवृषायध्वम् इति प्ण्डे पिण्डे ।
8.2.m: Having invoked the iḷā [and] consumed the drawn cups, after placing the Nārāśaṃsa cups, they throw southwards three balls each of sacrificial cake mixed with parched grains, per cup, at each ball [reciting]: 'Here, O Fathers, rejoice! According to your share, O Fathers, be bull-like!'

8.3.m: The [formula] 'devāya savitre' has already been mentioned.

8.3.s: hotā yakṣad devam savitāram iti praiṣaḥ |
8.3.d: होता यक्षद् देवम् सवितारम् इति प्रैषः ।
8.3.m: 'hotā yakṣad devam savitāram' is the ritual summons;

8.3.s: damūnā devaḥ savitā vareṇyo dadhad ratnam dakṣa pitṛbhya āyuni | pibāt somam amadann enam iṣṭayaḥ parijmā cid ramate asya dharmaṇi | iti yajati |
8.3.d: दमूना देवः सविता वरेण्यो दधद् रत्नम् दक्ष पितृभ्य आयुनि । पिबात् सोमम् अमदन्न् एनम् इष्टयः परिज्मा चिद् रमते अस्य धर्मणि । इति यजति ।
8.3.m: He recites the offering verse: / 'The domestic god Savitṛ, the desirable, / bestowing treasure on Dakṣa's fathers throughout life, / shall drink the soma. The sacrifices have rejoiced him; / he wandering about rests in his order.'

8.3.s: adhvaryo śośoṃsāvo ity āhāvaḥ śastra ādau tṛtīya savane sa ukthe |
8.3.d: अध्वर्यो शोशोंसावो इत्य् आहावः शस्त्र आदौ तृतीय सवने स उक्थे ।
8.3.m: 'adhvaryo śośoṃsāvaḥ' is the call at the beginning of a śastra in the third pressing if it includes the uktha;
That of the morning pressing is [used] within the śastra;

8.3.s: tat savitur vṛṇīmahe adyā no deva savitar iti tṛcau pratipad anucarau vaiśvadevasya |
8.3.d: तत् सवितुर् वृणीमहे अद्या नो देव सवितर् इति तृचौ प्रतिपद् अनुचरौ वैश्वदेवस्य ।
8.3.m: 'tat savitur vṛṇīmahe' [and] 'adyā no deva savitar' are the two triplets for the opening and the following verses of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra.
"abhūd devo" is the hymn to Savitṛ.

8.3.s: ekayā ca daśabhiś ca svabhūte dvābhyām iṣṭaye viṃśatī ca | tisṛbhiś ca vahase triṃśatā ca niyudbhir vāyav iha tā muñcaḥ |
8.3.d: एकया च दशभिश् च स्वभूते द्वाभ्याम् इष्टये विंशती च । तिसृभिश् च वहसे त्रिंशता च नियुद्भिर् वायव् इह ता मुञ्चः ।
8.3.m: "ekayā ca daśabhiś ca svabhūte dvābhyām iṣṭaye viṃśatī ca / tisṛbhiś ca vahase triṃśatā ca niyudbhir vāyav iha tā muñcaḥ" [is to Vāyu].

8.3.s: pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdha iti dyāvā pṛthivīyam |
8.3.d: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी ऋतावृध इति द्यावा पृथिवीयम् ।
8.3.m: "pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdhā" is the hymn to Heaven and Earth.
In this [hymn], the response contains the word 'mad'.
"takṣan ratham" is the hymn to the Ṛbhus.

8.3.s: ayam veno yebhyo mātā evā pitra ity eka pātinyaḥ |
8.3.d: अयम् वेनो येभ्यो माता एवा पित्र इत्य् एक पातिन्यः ।
8.3.m: "ayam veno", "yebhyo mātā", and "evā pitre" are single verses.

8.3.s: ā no bhadrā iti vaiśvadevasya uttame śiṣṭvā nividam |
8.3.d: आ नो भद्रा इति वैश्वदेवस्य उत्तमे शिष्ट्वा निविदम् ।
8.3.m: [The hymn] "ā no bhadrāḥ" belongs to the Viśve Devas; having left over the last [verse, he inserts] the nivid.
[He recites it] twice pāda by pāda, and for the third time by half-verse.

8.3.s: uktha vīryam japitvā viśve devāḥ śṛṇuta imam iti yajati |
8.3.d: उक्थ वीर्यम् जपित्वा विश्वे देवाः शृणुत इमम् इति यजति ।
8.3.m: Having muttered the ukthavīrya, he recites the offering verse: "viśve devāḥ śṛṇutemam".

8.4.s: ghṛtasya yaja ity ukto ghṛtam mimikṣa ity upāṃśu yajati |
8.4.d: घृतस्य यज इत्य् उक्तो घृतम् मिमिक्ष इत्य् उपांशु यजति ।
8.4.m: When instructed with "Recite the offering verse of the clarified butter", he recites the offering verse in a low voice: "ghṛtam mimikṣe".

8.4.s: saumyasya yaja ity uktas tvam soma pitṛbhir iti yajati |
8.4.d: सौम्यस्य यज इत्य् उक्तस् त्वम् सोम पितृभिर् इति यजति ।
8.4.m: When instructed with "Recite the offering verse of the Soma offering to the Fathers", he recites the offering verse: "tvam soma pitṛbhiḥ".

8.4.s: ghṛtasya yaja ity ukta | uru viṣṇo vi kramasva uru kṣayāya nas kṛdhi | ghṛta ghṛta yone piba pra pra yajña patim tira | ity upāṃśu yajati |
8.4.d: घृतस्य यज इत्य् उक्त । उरु विष्णो वि क्रमस्व उरु क्षयाय नस् कृधि । घृत घृत योने पिब प्र प्र यज्ञ पतिम् तिर । इत्य् उपांशु यजति ।
8.4.m: When instructed with "Recite the offering verse of the clarified butter", he recites the offering verse in a low voice: "uru viṣṇo vi kramasvoru kṣayāya nas kṛdhi / ghṛtaṃ ghṛtayone piba pra pra yajñapatiṃ tira".

8.4.s: saumyam hotā avekṣya aṅgulibhyām sarpir upaspṛśati |
8.4.d: सौम्यम् होता अवेक्ष्य अङ्गुलिभ्याम् सर्पिर् उपस्पृशति ।
8.4.m: The Hotṛ, having looked at the Soma offering to the Fathers, touches the clarified butter with two fingers.

8.4.s: cakṣuṣpā asi cakṣur me pāhi iti cakṣuṣī vimārṣṭi |
8.4.d: चक्षुष्पा असि चक्षुर् मे पाहि इति चक्षुषी विमार्ष्टि ।
8.4.m: With "cakṣuṣpā asi cakṣur me pāhi", he wipes his two eyes.

8.5.s: agnīt pātnīvatasya yaja ity ukta aibhir agne saratham ity upāṃśu yajati |
8.5.d: अग्नीत् पात्नीवतस्य यज इत्य् उक्त ऐभिर् अग्ने सरथम् इत्य् उपांशु यजति ।
8.5.m: When instructed with "Agnīdh, recite the offering verse for the Pātnīvata cup", he recites the offering verse in a low voice: "aibhir agne saratham".

8.5.s: abhakṣayitvā graham ādāya pūrvayā dvārā sadaḥ prapadya |
8.5.d: अभक्षयित्वा ग्रहम् आदाय पूर्वया द्वारा सदः प्रपद्य ।
8.5.m: Without partaking [of it], taking the cup, having entered the sadas by the eastern door,
having sat down near the Neṣṭṛ on the north,

8.6.m: the Yajñāyajñīya is the chant of the Āgnimāruta-śastra.
"vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase" is the hymn to Agni Vaiśvānara.
"pratvakṣasaḥ" is the hymn to the Maruts.

8.6.s: yajñā yajñā vo agnaye devo vo draviṇodā iti stotriya anurūpau pragāthau yajñāyajñīyasya |
8.6.d: यज्ञा यज्ञा वो अग्नये देवो वो द्रविणोदा इति स्तोत्रिय अनुरूपौ प्रगाथौ यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य ।
8.6.m: "yajñā yajñā vo agnaye" and "devo vo draviṇodāḥ" are the stotriya and anurūpa pragāthas of the Yajñāyajñīya [stotra].
"pra tavyasīm" is the hymn to Jātavedas.

8.6.s: uta no ahir budhnyaḥ śṛṇotv ity ekā |
8.6.d: उत नो अहिर् बुध्न्यः शृणोत्व् इत्य् एका ।
8.6.m: "uta no 'hir budhnyaḥ śṛṇotu" is a single verse.

8.6.s: avidad dakṣam ity akṣara paṅktayas tisraḥ |
8.6.d: अविदद् दक्षम् इत्य् अक्षर पङ्क्तयस् तिस्रः ।

8.6.m: There are three verses to the Fathers beginning with "ud īratām it".

8.6.s: imam yama mātalī kavyair aṅgirobhir iti yāmyaḥ |
8.6.d: इमम् यम मातली कव्यैर् अङ्गिरोभिर् इति याम्यः ।
8.6.m: "imam yama", "mātalī kavyaiḥ", and "aṅgirobhiḥ" are verses to Yama.

8.6.s: yayor ojasā viṣṇor nu kam tantum tanvann ity eka pātinyaḥ |
8.6.d: ययोर् ओजसा विष्णोर् नु कम् तन्तुम् तन्वन्न् इत्य् एक पातिन्यः ।
8.6.m: "yayor ojasā", "viṣṇor nu kam", and "tantum tanvan" are single verses.

8.6.s: evā na indro maghavā iti paridhāya uktha vīryam japitvā agne marudbhiḥ śubhayadbhir iti yajati |
8.6.d: एवा न इन्द्रो मघवा इति परिधाय उक्थ वीर्यम् जपित्वा अग्ने मरुद्भिः शुभयद्भिर् इति यजति ।
8.6.m: Having concluded with "evā na indro maghavā", [and] having muttered the ukthavīrya, he recites the offering verse: "agne marudbhiḥ śubhayadbhiḥ".

8.7.m: The first nivid belongs to the Marutvatīya-śastra.
The second belongs to the Niṣkevalya-śastra.
The third and following belong to the Vaiśvadeva and Āgnimāruta śastras.
As many hymns as there are, so many are the nivids.
Before each hymn there is a call (āhāva),
and in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, before the pratipad and the anucara [tṛcas],
and in the Āgnimāruta-śastra, before the stotriya and anurūpa [pragāthas],
The śastra of the Vaiśvadeva is separated.

8.7.s: abhyagram āgnimārutasya āpo hi ṣṭhīyāḥ parihāpya |
8.7.d: अभ्यग्रम् आग्निमारुतस्य आपो हि ष्ठीयाः परिहाप्य ।
8.7.m: [They do so] at the beginning of the Āgnimāruta-śastra, leaving out the verses beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭhā".

8.7.s: apsu somān sādayitvā anuyāja ādi śamyv antam paśu karma kṛtvā hāriyojanena caranti |
8.7.d: अप्सु सोमान् सादयित्वा अनुयाज आदि शम्य्व् अन्तम् पशु कर्म कृत्वा हारियोजनेन चरन्ति ।
8.7.m: Having placed the soma-cups in water, having performed the animal rite beginning with the after-offerings and ending with the Śaṃyu-formula, they proceed with the Hāriyojana-cup.

8.8.m: “tiṣṭhā su kam” is the introductory verse.
“dhānāḥ somānām indra it” is the ritual summons.

8.8.s: dhānāḥ somānām agne vīhi ity anuvaṣaṭ kāraḥ |
8.8.d: धानाः सोमानाम् अग्ने वीहि इत्य् अनुवषट् कारः ।
8.8.m: “dhānāḥ somānām agne vīhi” is the secondary vaṣaṭ-call.

8.8.s: apṣu dhūtasya deva soma te mativido nṛbhi ṣṭuta stotrasya śasta ukthasya iṣṭa yajuṣo yo aśvasanir gosanir bhakṣas tasya ta upahūtasya upahūto bhakṣayāmi iti prāṇa bhakṣān bhakṣayitvā dhānā vyādadhate |
8.8.d: अप्षु धूतस्य देव सोम ते मतिविदो नृभि ष्टुत स्तोत्रस्य शस्त उक्थस्य इष्ट यजुषो यो अश्वसनिर् गोसनिर् भक्षस् तस्य त उपहूतस्य उपहूतो भक्षयामि इति प्राण भक्षान् भक्षयित्वा धाना व्यादधते ।
8.8.m: Having consumed [their shares] by smelling them with: “Of you, divine Soma, washed in water, who know the mind, whose praise has been sung by men with a chant, whose recitation has been uttered in a śastra, whose Yajus has been offered, who grant horses and cattle—of you, summoned, being summoned I consume,” they take portions of parched barley-grain.
The Hotṛ should obtain the largest portion.

8.8.s: yathā ha tyad vasava iti dhiṣṇyān samīkṣya āgnīdhrīyam uttareṇa āhavanīyam āyanti |
8.8.d: यथा ह त्यद् वसव इति धिष्ण्यान् समीक्ष्य आग्नीध्रीयम् उत्तरेण आहवनीयम् आयन्ति ।
8.8.m: Having looked upon the dhiṣṇya-hearths with: “yathā ha tyad vasavaḥ,” they come north of the Āgnīdhra fire toward the Āhavanīya fire.

8.8.s: bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā sa tvam no agne avamas tvam no agne varuṇasya tad astu mitrā varuṇā ity āgnīdhrīye prāyaś citta āhutīr juhvati |
8.8.d: भूर् भुवः स्वः स्वाहा स त्वम् नो अग्ने अवमस् त्वम् नो अग्ने वरुणस्य तद् अस्तु मित्रा वरुणा इत्य् आग्नीध्रीये प्रायश् चित्त आहुतीर् जुह्वति ।
8.8.m: They offer expiatory oblations in the Āgnīdhra fire with: “bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā,” “sa tvam no agne avamaḥ,” “tvam no agne varuṇasya,” and “tad astu mitrāvaruṇā.”

8.8.s: āpura stā mā prajayā paśubhiḥ pūrayata ity āhavanīyasya bhasma ante dhānā nyupya pañca pañca śakalān ādadhate |
8.8.d: आपुर स्ता मा प्रजया पशुभिः पूरयत इत्य् आहवनीयस्य भस्म अन्ते धाना न्युप्य पञ्च पञ्च शकलान् आदधते ।
8.8.m: Having scattered parched barley-grain at the border of the ashes of the Āhavanīya fire with: “O full ones, fill me with offspring and cattle,” they put on [the fire] five wood splinters each,

8.9.s: ātma kṛtasya enaso avayajanam asi manuṣya kṛtasya enaso avayajanam asi pitṛ kṛtasya enaso avayajanam asi deva kṛtasya enaso avayajanam asi yac ca aham eno vidvāṃś cakāra yac ca avidvāṃs tasya sarvasya avayajanam asi iti |
8.9.d: आत्म कृतस्य एनसो अवयजनम् असि मनुष्य कृतस्य एनसो अवयजनम् असि पितृ कृतस्य एनसो अवयजनम् असि देव कृतस्य एनसो अवयजनम् असि यच् च अहम् एनो विद्वांश् चकार यच् च अविद्वांस् तस्य सर्वस्य अवयजनम् असि इति ।
8.9.m: with: “You are an expiation for sin committed by oneself; you are an expiation for sin committed by men; you are an expiation for sin committed by the fathers; you are an expiation for sin committed by the gods; and whatever sin I have committed knowingly and whatever unknowingly, of all that you are the expiation.”

8.9.s: savya āvṛta uttareṇa āhavanīyam apsu somān yathā camasam paścād upopaviśya pavitrāṇy avadhāya ceṣṭayante | sam āpo adbhir agmata sam oṣadhayo rasena | sam revatīr jagatībhiḥ pṛcyantām sma madhumatīr madhumatībhiḥ pṛcyantām iti |
8.9.d: सव्य आवृत उत्तरेण आहवनीयम् अप्सु सोमान् यथा चमसम् पश्चाद् उपोपविश्य पवित्राण्य् अवधाय चेष्टयन्ते । सम् आपो अद्भिर् अग्मत सम् ओषधयो रसेन । सम् रेवतीर् जगतीभिः पृच्यन्ताम् स्म मधुमतीर् मधुमतीभिः पृच्यन्ताम् इति ।
8.9.m: Turning to the left, sitting down behind the soma-portions in water north of the Āhavanīya fire each beside his cup, and inserting purifying strainers, they stir [the water] with: “The waters have united with the waters; the plants with juice; may the wealthy waters unite with the Jagatī metres; may the honeyed ones mingle with the honeyed ones.”

8.9.s: apsu dhūtasya deva soma te mativido yo aśvasanir gosanir bhakṣas tasya ta upahūtasya upahūto bhakṣayāmi iti prāṇa bhakṣān bhakṣayitvā |
8.9.d: अप्सु धूतस्य देव सोम ते मतिविदो यो अश्वसनिर् गोसनिर् भक्षस् तस्य त उपहूतस्य उपहूतो भक्षयामि इति प्राण भक्षान् भक्षयित्वा ।
8.9.m: Having consumed [their shares] by smelling with: “Of you, divine Soma, washed in water, who know the mind, who grant horses and cattle—of you, summoned, being summoned I consume,”

8.9.s: acchāyam vo yayor ojasā iti prācīr ninīya udīcīr vā |
8.9.d: अच्छायम् वो ययोर् ओजसा इति प्राचीर् निनीय उदीचीर् वा ।
8.9.m: and having poured [the water] out toward the east or toward the north with: “acchāyam vo yayor ojasā,”
and having addressed it with: “samudram vaḥ,”

8.9.s: śam no devīyābhiś catasṛbhir uro abhimṛśya |
8.9.d: शम् नो देवीयाभिश् चतसृभिर् उरो अभिमृश्य ।
8.9.m: and having touched the chest with the four verses beginning with: “śam no devīḥ,”

8.9.s: samānam prāṇa sammarśanam mukha vimārjanam ca |
8.9.d: समानम् प्राण सम्मर्शनम् मुख विमार्जनम् च ।
8.9.m: the touching of the breaths and the wiping of the mouth are the same [as taught before].

8.9.s: dakṣiṇa āvṛta āgnīdhrīye dadhi prāśya yathā dadhi bhakṣam |
8.9.d: दक्षिण आवृत आग्नीध्रीये दधि प्राश्य यथा दधि भक्षम् ।
8.9.m: Turning to the right, having eaten curd at the Āgnīdhra fire according to the rule of consuming curd;

8.9.s: patnī samyājān saṃsthāpya huteṣu samiṣṭa yajuhṣu avabhṛtam avaiti |
8.9.d: पत्नी सम्याजान् संस्थाप्य हुतेषु समिष्ट यजुह्षु अवभृतम् अवैति ।
8.9.m: having concluded the offerings to the wives of the gods, when the concluding oblations have been offered, he goes down to the purificatory bath.

8.10.s: punar mām aitv indriyam punar ātmā draviṇam brāhmaṇam ca | punar agnayo dhiṣṇyāso yathā sthānam dhārayantām iha eva | iti yajamāno dhiṣṇyān samīkṣya atra anūbandhyāyām vā saṃsthitāyām ṛtvijaḥ samīkṣeta | ubhā kavī yuvānā satyādā dharmaṇā satyasya dharmaṇas patī vi sakhyāni sṛjāmahai | iti |
8.10.d: पुनर् माम् ऐत्व् इन्द्रियम् पुनर् आत्मा द्रविणम् ब्राह्मणम् च । पुनर् अग्नयो धिष्ण्यासो यथा स्थानम् धारयन्ताम् इह एव । इति यजमानो धिष्ण्यान् समीक्ष्य अत्र अनूबन्ध्यायाम् वा संस्थितायाम् ऋत्विजः समीक्षेत । उभा कवी युवाना सत्यादा धर्मणा सत्यस्य धर्मणस् पती वि सख्यानि सृजामहै । इति ।
8.10.m:
With: “May virile power come back to me, again spirit, wealth, and priestly rank; may the fire-hearths again hold themselves each in its place here,” the sacrificer, having looked upon the dhiṣṇya-hearths here or when the subsequently bound victim is concluded, should look upon the priests,
[saying:] “Both wise, youthful, true to law, lords of true law, let us break up our friendships.”
[The Hotṛ] follows along reciting: “urum hi rājā.”
All join in the finale of the Sāman.

8.10.s: namo varuṇāya ahbiṣṭhito varuṇasya pāśa ity apsu pādam avadhāya |
8.10.d: नमो वरुणाय अह्बिष्ठितो वरुणस्य पाश इत्य् अप्सु पादम् अवधाय ।
8.10.m: Having placed a foot in the water with: “Homage to Varuṇa! Trodden upon is Varuṇa's noose,”

8.11.s: apṣv agne apṣu me soma iti vā apsumantau |
8.11.d: अप्ष्व् अग्ने अप्षु मे सोम इति वा अप्सुमन्तौ ।
8.11.m: Or the two verses containing the word apsu are: “apsv agne” and “apsu me somaḥ.”

8.11.s: ud uttamam varuṇa ava te heḷaḥ |
8.11.d: उद् उत्तमम् वरुण अव ते हेऌअः ।
8.11.m: “ud uttamam varuṇa” and “ava te heḷaḥ” [are the introductory and consecratory verses for Varuṇa].

8.11.s: sa tvam no agne avamas tvam no agne varuṇasya vidvān ity agnī varuṇāv ādiśati |
8.11.d: स त्वम् नो अग्ने अवमस् त्वम् नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वान् इत्य् अग्नी वरुणाव् आदिशति ।
8.11.m: With: “sa tvam no agne avamaḥ” and “tvam no agne varuṇasya vidvān,” he designates Agni and Varuṇa.
He recites the offering verses for the fore-offerings and after-offerings without [the one to] the sacrificial grass.
[The iṣṭi] begins with the fore-offerings and ends with the after-offerings,

8.11.s: ājya bhāgau vā parihāpya anuyājau ca |
8.11.d: आज्य भागौ वा परिहाप्य अनुयाजौ च ।
8.11.m: or omitting the two portions of clarified butter and the two after-offerings.

8.11.s: yena striyāv akurutam yena apāmṛśatam surām yenā kṣām abhyaṣiñcatam yena imām pṛthivīm mahīm yad vām tad aśvinā yaśas tena mām abhiṣiñcatam | iti hotā abhyukṣate |
8.11.d: येन स्त्रियाव् अकुरुतम् येन अपामृशतम् सुराम् येना क्षाम् अभ्यषिञ्चतम् येन इमाम् पृथिवीम् महीम् यद् वाम् तद् अश्विना यशस् तेन माम् अभिषिञ्चतम् । इति होता अभ्युक्षते ।
8.11.m: The Hotṛ sprinkles himself with: “With that glory by which you two made two women, by which you wiped away surā, by which you anointed the dice, by which this great earth—with that, O Aśvins, anoint me.”

8.11.s: upa ucchivena cakṣuṣā gṛhān paraimi mānuṣaḥ | ity āgacchan yajamānaḥ |
8.11.d: उप उच्छिवेन चक्षुषा गृहान् परैमि मानुषः । इत्य् आगच्छन् यजमानः ।
8.11.m: Returning, the sacrificer [recites]: “With an auspicious eye I, a mortal, come home.”

8.11.s: iho sahasra dakṣiṇo api pūṣā ni ṣīdatu | ity upaviśya āhavanīye samidhāv ādadhāti devānām samid asi iti pūrvām tūṣṇīm uttarām |
8.11.d: इहो सहस्र दक्षिणो अपि पूषा नि षीदतु । इत्य् उपविश्य आहवनीये समिधाव् आदधाति देवानाम् समिद् असि इति पूर्वाम् तूष्णीम् उत्तराम् ।
8.11.m: Having sat down with: “Here also may Pūṣan of a thousand priestly gifts sit,” he places two kindling-sticks on the Āhavanīya fire: the first with: “You are the kindling-stick of the gods,” and the second silently.
The sacrificer's wife [places two kindling-sticks] silently on the Gārhapatya fire.

8.12.m: By the introductory rite the concluding rite is explained.
There is an inversion of the consecratory and introductory verses, except for the Sviṣṭakṛt.
He recites the offering verse to Pathyā Svasti as the fourth,
And there is a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa as the subsequently bound victim,

8.12.s: ā vām mitrā varuṇā tat su vām mitrā varuṇā o mitrā varuṇā iti puronuvākyāḥ |
8.12.d: आ वाम् मित्रा वरुणा तत् सु वाम् मित्रा वरुणा ओ मित्रा वरुणा इति पुरोनुवाक्याः ।
8.12.m: “ā vām mitrāvaruṇā,” “tat su vām mitrāvaruṇā,” and “o mitrāvaruṇā” are the introductory verses.

8.12.s: yuvam vastrāṇi yad banhiṣṭham pra bāhava iti yājyāḥ |
8.12.d: युवम् वस्त्राणि यद् बन्हिष्ठम् प्र बाहव इति याज्याः ।

8.12.s: dīkṣaṇīyā prabhṛtyā anubandhyāyāḥ saṃsthānān na vede patnīm vācayati na stṛṇāti |
